<?php
// config/rdvmedecins.php: application-specific settings, read by
// config('rdvmedecins.xxx'). The values come from the .env file; the second
// env() parameter is the default value
return [
    'jwt' => [
         // secret key for tokens JWT: at least 32 characters (HMAC-SHA256)
        'secret' => env('JWT_SECRET', ''),
         // token validity period, in minutes; the cookie that carries it
         // has the same lifetime
        'duree' => (int) env('JWT_DUREE_MINUTES', 120),
    ],

     // true: SQL commands sent to the database are displayed in the console
    'db_log' => (bool) env('DB_LOG', false),

     // true in production (HTTPS): cookies are never sent in plain text
    'cookie_secure' => (bool) env('COOKIE_SECURE', false),

     // bot protection (see app/Auth/LimiteurTentatives.php):
     // login: a certain number of failed login attempts are allowed for the same username from the same IP address (IP),
     // followed by a lockout for this duration (the entire address IP is also blocked
     // if it accumulates 5 times more failed attempts, across all logins)
    'login_max_echecs' => (int) env('LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS', 5),
    'login_blocage_minutes' => (int) env('LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES', 15),
     // customer account creation: maximum number of accounts created per hour per address
     // IP. In a classroom, all workstations often connect via the same IP address:
     // Increase if necessary
    'inscription_max_par_heure' => (int) env('INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE', 10),
];

Application-specific settings, read by [config('rdvmedecins.jwt.secret')], [config('rdvmedecins.login_max_echecs')]... Each value comes from the file [.env], with a default value. Recall the rule (Example 25): [env] is called only in files within the [config] folder; the rest of the code reads [config(...)]. Once the configuration is cached ([php artisan config:cache]), the file [.env] is no longer read at all.

docs.title: 11.7.1. public/index.php and bootstrap/providers.php
docs.text:
The file [public/index.php] is the one from the examples (Example 01), with the path to the application’s [vendor] folder:

<?php
// public/index.php: the entry point for TOUTES requests to HTTP. The folder
// [public] is the site root: only its files are accessible from the
// browser (Bootstrap, stylesheet, script); the application code is never accessible

use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

// Composer’s class loader
require __DIR__.'/../vendor/autoload.php';

// the application, built by bootstrap/app.php, processes the current request
/** @var Application $app */
$app = require_once __DIR__.'/../bootstrap/app.php';
$app->handleRequest(Request::capture());

The file [bootstrap/providers.php] is new:

<?php
// bootstrap/providers.php: the service providers for
// the application, loaded when each request starts (see app/Providers)

use App\Providers\AppServiceProvider;

return [
    AppServiceProvider::class,
];

It returns the list of service providers for the application. A service provider is a class for which [Laravel] calls two methods at the start of each request: [register], which registers services with the container (example 06), and then, once all providers are registered, [boot], which can use any service. [Laravel] itself is composed of service providers (one for the session, one for views, one for the database, etc.), as are most of the libraries written for it. In the examples, we wrote these declarations in [bootstrap/app.php] ([withSingletons], [booted]): This is convenient for a few lines; a full-scale application groups them into a service provider, [AppServiceProvider] by convention.

docs.title: 11.7.2. app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php: the application’s FOURNISSEUR DE SERVICES
// (declared in bootstrap/providers.php). This is the standard location in a
// Laravel application, as described in the examples in bootstrap/app.php:
//    - $singletons: shared services (see Example 06);
//    - boot(): what must be done at the start of each request, once all
//      registered services: the authentication driver JWT, the variables
//      shared by all views, the display of commands SQL.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Providers;

use App\Auth\AuthService;
use App\Auth\CaptchaService;
use App\Auth\LimiteurTentatives;
use App\Auth\PasseInscription;
use App\Dao\ClientDao;
use App\Dao\CreneauDao;
use App\Dao\MedecinDao;
use App\Dao\RvDao;
use App\Dao\UserDao;
use App\Metier\MetierService;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use Illuminate\Database\Events\QueryExecuted;
use Illuminate\Database\Events\TransactionBeginning;
use Illuminate\Database\Events\TransactionCommitted;
use Illuminate\Database\Events\TransactionRolledBack;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\App;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cookie;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\View;
use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;
use Illuminate\View\View as LaVue;

class AppServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // shared services: for each of these classes, the Laravel container
     // creates only one UN object (per request), which is provided to all who request it—the
     // controllers, via their constructors. The container itself creates the
     // dependencies for each one (MetierService thus receives its five DAO): this is
     // dependency injection.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public array $singletons = [
        MedecinDao::class => MedecinDao::class,
        ClientDao::class => ClientDao::class,
        CreneauDao::class => CreneauDao::class,
        RvDao::class => RvDao::class,
        UserDao::class => UserDao::class,
        MetierService::class => MetierService::class,
        ApplicationModel::class => ApplicationModel::class,
        AuthService::class => AuthService::class,
        CaptchaService::class => CaptchaService::class,
        LimiteurTentatives::class => LimiteurTentatives::class,
        PasseInscription::class => PasseInscription::class,
    ];

    public function boot(): void
    {
         // ---- the watcher driver [jwt] (see config/auth.php, Example 25): a
         // a function that receives the request and returns the authenticated user, or null
         // for an anonymous visitor. Laravel calls it on the first Auth::user() in the
         // request; if it finds a user, it keeps that user for the rest of the
         // request (otherwise, it calls the function every time Auth::user() is called)
        Auth::viaRequest('jwt', function (Request $request) {
            $jeton = $request->cookie(AuthService::COOKIE);
            if (! is_string($jeton) || $jeton === '') {
                return null;
            }
            $utilisateur = app(AuthService::class)->utilisateur($jeton);
            if ($utilisateur === null) {
                 // a cookie is present but invalid (expired or forged token): it is deleted
                Cookie::queue(AuthService::cookieEffacement());
            }
            return $utilisateur;
        });

         // ---- variables common to all views (see Example 15): a
         // "view composer" is executed before each view is rendered ('*')
            // - user: the logged-in user (or null), for the navigation bar;
            //       - language : "fr" or "en".
        View::composer('*', function (LaVue $vue) {
            $vue->with(['utilisateur' => Auth::user(), 'langue' => App::getLocale()]);
        });

         // ---- DB_LOG=true (.env file): each SQL command, and each step of a
         // transaction is displayed in the server console (see Example 28)
        if (config('rdvmedecins.db_log')) {
            DB::listen(fn (QueryExecuted $q) => error_log($q->sql.' '.json_encode($q->bindings, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE)));
            Event::listen(TransactionBeginning::class, fn () => error_log('BEGIN'));
            Event::listen(TransactionCommitted::class, fn () => error_log('COMMIT'));
            Event::listen(TransactionRolledBack::class, fn () => error_log('ROLLBACK'));
        }
    }
}
  • Lines 48–60: shared services. The [$singletons] property of a service provider is read by [Laravel], which declares each of its [interface => classe] pairs as a singleton (Example 06): This is equivalent to [withSingletons]. Here, each class is declared on its own. Remember that a singleton exists only for the duration of a single request (Example 06): the benefit here is that all controllers, middleware, and services within the same request share the same [ApplicationModel], the same [MetierService]... The DAO instances might not even be declared: the container knows how to create a class that hasn’t been declared (Example 06), but it would create a new object for each request;
  • lines 69–80: the watchdog driver [jwt] (example 25). The token is read from the [rdvmedecins_jwt] cookie (the name is a constant from [AuthService]) and verified by [AuthService::utilisateur]. A cookie that exists but whose token is no longer valid is deleted. [Laravel] retains the user found for the entire request; as long as it has not found one (an anonymous visitor), it calls the function with each request, which has no impact: reading a cookie and, if necessary, verifying a signature, is very fast;
  • Lines 86–88: variables common to all views (Example 15): the logged-in user (or [null]), for the navigation bar, and the request language. The pattern ['*'] matches all views: the composer is called for each one, including fragments and components;
  • Lines 92–99: Display of SQL orders and transactions in the console (Example 28), if [DB_LOG=true]. [error_log] writes to the error log of [PHP]—that is, along with [php artisan serve], in the server console.

docs.title: 11.7.3. bootstrap/app.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// bootstrap/app.php: the application build (see Example 01):
//    1. Routes (routes/web.php);
//    2. middleware: language, cookies, authentication, roles;
//    3. Exceptions: how errors are converted into pages HTML.
// Shared services are declared in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php.
// =========================================================================

use App\Auth\AuthService;
use App\Auth\SessionInvalide;
use App\Http\Middleware\ExigerRoles;
use App\Http\Middleware\FixerLangue;
use App\Http\Middleware\VerifierPasseInscription;
use App\Web\Flash;
use Illuminate\Auth\AuthenticationException;
use Illuminate\Auth\Middleware\Authenticate;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Configuration\Exceptions;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Configuration\Middleware;
use Illuminate\Http\Exceptions\HttpResponseException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\ViewErrorBag;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpExceptionInterface;

return Application::configure(basePath: dirname(__DIR__))
    ->withRouting(web: __DIR__.'/../routes/web.php')

    ->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware): void {
         // The request language: a GLOBAL middleware, executed for all
         // requests, before those in the [web] group (see app/Http/Middleware/FixerLangue.php)
        $middleware->append(FixerLangue::class);

         // Laravel CHIFFRE all the cookies it sets. Two exceptions: the token
         // JWT, which is already signed; and the language, which is read before the cookies are decrypted
        $middleware->encryptCookies(except: [AuthService::COOKIE, FixerLangue::COOKIE]);

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
         // LA RÈGLE D'ACCÈS: all routes in the [web] group require an
         // an authenticated user (Authenticate middleware, also known as [auth])—except
         // those that explicitly waive this requirement (withoutMiddleware, see
         // routes/web.php: login, account creation, language selection).
         // This is the “everything is prohibited unless explicitly permitted” rule: a route
         // added later—even if we forgot to protect it—is automatically protected.
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        $middleware->web(append: [Authenticate::class]);

         // An unauthenticated visitor requesting a protected page is redirected to the
         // login page. If they had a token cookie, it means their token
         // is no longer valid (expired, tampered with): their session has expired, and they are notified
        $middleware->redirectGuestsTo(function (Request $request) {
            if ($request->cookie(AuthService::COOKIE)) {
                Flash::erreur('ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
            }
            return route('login');
        });

         // Short names (aliases) for the middleware used in routes/web.php
        $middleware->alias([
            'role' => ExigerRoles::class,
            'passe.inscription' => VerifierPasseInscription::class,
        ]);
    })

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // How errors become pages HTML (see Example 24). Three cases:
        // 1. a SessionInvalide (account deleted since login) -> return to the
           // login page, as with an expired session;
        // 2. an error HTTP: abort(400), abort(403) (insufficient role),
           // unknown (404), unsupported method (405), missing or invalid anti-CSRF token
           // missing or invalid (419)... -> the error page, with the original code;
        // 3. any other exception (a true error): Laravel logs it to the
           // log (storage/logs/laravel.log), along with its call stack; in
           // production (APP_DEBUG=false), the user sees the 500 error page—
           // never the call stack; in development, the Laravel debug page.
     // A render function that returns null causes Laravel to handle the exception in its
     // way.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    ->withExceptions(function (Exceptions $exceptions): void {
         // the error page. $errors: the input error variable, which all
         // views can read, does not yet exist if the error occurred
         // before the middleware that creates it (a 405 page, for example)
        $pageErreur = function (int $code) {
            $message = match ($code) {
                400 => 'ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST',
                403 => 'ERRORS.FORBIDDEN',
                404 => 'ERRORS.NOT_FOUND',
                419 => 'ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED',
                default => 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
            };
            return response()->view('erreur', ['titrePage' => 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE', 'code' => $code,
                'message' => $message, 'errors' => new ViewErrorBag], $code);
        };

        $exceptions->render(function (SessionInvalide $e) {
            Flash::erreur('ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
            return redirect()->route('login')->withCookie(AuthService::cookieEffacement());
        });

        $exceptions->render(fn (HttpExceptionInterface $e) => $pageErreur($e->getStatusCode()));

        $exceptions->render(function (Throwable $e) use ($pageErreur) {
             // These exceptions are handled separately: redirection to the
             // login page (AuthenticationException), return to the form with the
             // input errors (ValidationException)...
            if (config('app.debug') || $e instanceof AuthenticationException
                || $e instanceof ValidationException || $e instanceof HttpResponseException) {
                return null;
            }
            return $pageErreur(500);
        });
    })
    ->create();

The file that builds the application (Example 01). It contains everything related to request handling: routes, middleware, and exceptions.

  • line 28: the routes ([routes/web.php], discussed later);
  • line 33: the request language is set by a global middleware (example 24), which is executed for all requests, even before routing;
  • line 37: [Laravel] encrypts all cookies (Example 20), except for those that are excluded: the JWT token, which is already signed (Example 25), and the language. The language cookie is read by a global middleware, which runs before the [EncryptCookies] middleware in the [web] group: it must therefore be readable without decryption. Why use a global middleware rather than a middleware from the [web] group? So that even requests that do not result in a route (a 405 page) display their error page in the correct language;
  • Line 47: the application’s access rule. The [Authenticate] middleware (the [auth] alias from Example 25) is added to the [web] group, i.e., to all routes. A public route (the login page, account creation, language selection) must explicitly remove it using [withoutMiddleware] (within [routes/web.php]). This follows the rule “everything is prohibited unless explicitly permitted”: a route added later—even if you forgot to protect it—is automatically protected. The opposite error (a public route you forgot to open) is immediately apparent; the error of a forgotten protected page is much less so;
  • Lines 52–57: An unauthenticated visitor who requests a protected page is redirected to the login page. If the visitor’s browser sent a token cookie, it means that token is no longer valid (expired or tampered with): the visitor is notified via a pop-up message ([Flash::erreur], discussed later). [redirectGuestsTo] accepts a URL, or a function that receives the request and returns the URL;
  • Lines 60–63: aliases (short names) for route middleware: [role] and [passe.inscription], used in [routes/web.php].

Lines 80–113 convert errors into HTML pages (Example 24):

  • Lines 84–91: the function that generates the error page for code HTTP: the view [erreur], the code, the message key, and the response code HTTP. A subtle point: the application views read the variable [$errors] (input errors, Example 19), which the [ShareErrorsFromSession] middleware in the [web] group shares with all views. An error that occurs before this middleware (an unsupported HTTP method, 405, is detected by the router) would reach a view without [$errors]: an empty one ([new ViewErrorBag]) is provided to it;
  • lines 96–99: the [SessionInvalide] exception (the token account no longer exists; see below): return to the login page, token cookie cleared, with the message “session expired”;
  • line 101: all errors HTTP—[abort(403)], [abort(404)], an unknown route, an unsupported method, a missing or invalid anti-CSRF token (419, example 18)... become the error page, along with their codes;
  • Lines 103–112: Any other exception is a true anomaly (the database is inaccessible, a programming error...). [Laravel] always logs it in the [storage/logs/laravel.log] log, along with its call stack. In production ([APP_DEBUG=false]), the user sees the 500 error page—never the call stack, which would reveal the application’s code to a hacker; in development, the function returns [null]: [Laravel] displays its debug page. Note: [Throwable] handles all exceptions, including those that [Laravel] handles itself, and these should be left to it: [AuthenticationException] (an unauthenticated visitor, redirected to [/login]), [ValidationException] (an invalid input, returned to the form, example 19), [HttpResponseException] (an exception that carries its own response). The rendering functions are tried in the order in which they are declared: errors HTTP have already been handled by the previous one.

docs.title: 11.8. The templates
docs.text: The [Eloquent] templates (example 28): one class per table.

docs.title: 11.8.1. app/Models/Role.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Models/Role.php: a user’s three roles (column users.role):
//    - ADMI N: the administrator—appointments + management of doctors and clients;
//    - DOCTOR: a doctor—books and cancels appointments;
//    - USE  R : a client (patient)—books appointments for themselves, manages their account.
// A “backed” enum: each case has a value, the string
// is stored as-is in the database; Role::from('ADMIN') performs the reverse process

namespace App\Models;

enum Role: string
{
    case ADMIN = 'ADMIN';
    case DOCTOR = 'DOCTOR';
    case USER = 'USER';
}

The three roles, in the form of an enumeration ([enum], [PHP] 8.1): a type whose only possible values are its cases: [Role::ADMIN], [Role::DOCTOR], and [Role::USER]. A variable of type [Role] cannot contain ['ADMINN']: the typo is detected. [enum Role: string] declares a backed enumeration: each case has a value, in this case the base-sorted string. [Role::ADMIN->value] is equal to ['ADMIN']; [Role::from('ADMIN')] returns the corresponding case (and throws an exception for an unknown value); [Role::tryFrom(...)] returns [null] in this case.

docs.title: 11.8.2. app/Models/User.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Models/User.php: a user authorized to log in (table [users]).
// Each doctor and each client has a SON account (column [user] in the tables
// [medecins] and [clients]; see Personne.php).
//
// Uniqueness constraint SQL: unq_users_login (a login belongs to only one
// account). It is created by the script database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql; the
// business layer recognizes it by its NOM (see app/Metier/MetierService.php).

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

class User extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'users';

     // The table does not have the columns created_at / updated_at that Eloquent manages by default
    public $timestamps = false;

     // columns that can be populated in bulk (User::create([...]), new User([...]))
    protected $fillable = ['login', 'password', 'nom', 'role'];

     // the password HACHÉ (bcrypt) never leaves the object if it is converted to
     // an array or to JSON
    protected $hidden = ['password'];

     // conversions: the column [role] (text) becomes a Role, and vice versa
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['role' => Role::class, 'version' => 'integer'];
    }
}
  • line 16: the table. [Eloquent] would have guessed it (the class name, in lowercase, in the English plural: [users]); we write it out everywhere for clarity;
  • Line 19: No table in the database has the columns [created_at] and [updated_at], which [Eloquent] populates by default (Example 28);
  • line 22: the columns that can be filled in bulk using [User::create([...])] (example 28);
  • line 26: the password hash will not appear if the object is converted to an array or to JSON ([$user->toArray()]): a precaution;
  • Lines 29–32: the conversions (Example 28): the column [role] (text) becomes [Role] when read, and vice versa when written: [$user->role] is [Role], never a string. The column [version] is read as an integer: the [PDO] driver for [MySQL] can render numbers as strings, and the business layer’s strict comparison of [$version !== $personne->version] would fail.

docs.title: 11.8.3. app/Models/Personne.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Models/Personne.php: what doctors (table [medecins]) and
// clients (table [clients]) have in common: a title, a last name, a first name—and the associated
// associated user account (column [user]).
//
// Both tables have exactly the same columns: they are described UNE times,
// in this class ABSTRAITE (a "Person" is never created), from which
// "Doctor" and "Client"; each specifies only the name of its table.
//
// Note: [Client] refers here to a PATIENT from the medical practice, not a client
// HTTP! This is the original business domain vocabulary, retained as-is.

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

abstract class Personne extends Model
{
    public $timestamps = false;

     // [user] is the name of the foreign key column -> users(id): a simple
     // number, the account ID ($medecin->user)
    protected $fillable = ['titre', 'nom', 'prenom', 'user'];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['user' => 'integer', 'version' => 'integer'];
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // The RELATION linked to the user account: a person has the UN account, identified
     // by the foreign key [user]. belongsTo: "belongs to"—the foreign key
     // is in the CETTE table. $medecin->account is then a User object, retrieved from the database
     // on the first access, or as soon as the query with 'account' is executed (see app/Dao).
     // The relation cannot be named [user]: that name is already used for the
     // column, and $medecin->user refers to the column.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function compte(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'user');
    }

     // "Ms. Alice DURAND"
    public function libelle(): string
    {
        return "{$this->titre} {$this->prenom} {$this->nom}";
    }
}

The tables [medecins] and [clients] have the same columns. Their common description is written once, in an abstract class ([abstract class]): a class for which no objects are ever created, serving only as a base class for inheritance. The classes [Medecin] and [Client] inherit from it and specify only the name of their table.

  • Line 24: [user] is the foreign key column; [$medecin->user] is a simple number, the account ID;
  • Lines 39–42: the relationship to the account. A relationship [Eloquent] is a method that describes the link between two tables; [belongsTo] (“belongs to”) describes a foreign key in this table: [belongsTo(User::class, 'user')] specifies that the column [user] contains the ID of a [User]. It is used as a property: [$medecin->compte] is the object [User]. [Eloquent] reads it from the database on the first access (this is called *lazy loading*), or as soon as the query that retrieves the doctor requests it (if necessary; *eager loading*, see [with('compte')] in the DAO layer). The relation cannot be named [user]: [$medecin->user] already refers to the column, and [Eloquent] gives priority to the columns;
  • Lines 45–48: a person’s name, “Ms. Alice DURAND,” used by all pages. In a string enclosed in quotation marks, [{$this->titre}] inserts the value of a property.

class Medecin extends Personne

docs.title: 11.8.5. app/Models/Creneau.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Models/Creneau.php: a doctor’s time slot (table [creneaux]):
// 8:00 a.m. – 8:20 a.m., etc.

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

class Creneau extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'creneaux';

    public $timestamps = false;

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['id_medecin' => 'integer', 'hdebut' => 'integer', 'mdebut' => 'integer',
            'hfin' => 'integer', 'mfin' => 'integer', 'version' => 'integer'];
    }

     // multiple time slots for the same doctor: the foreign key [id_medecin]
    public function medecin(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Medecin::class, 'id_medecin');
    }

     // "8:00 - 8:20"; sprintf('%02d'): "8:05" rather than "8:5"
    public function horaire(): string
    {
        return sprintf('%d:%02d - %d:%02d', $this->hdebut, $this->mdebut, $this->hfin, $this->mfin);
    }
}
  • lines 23–26: the relationship to the doctor for the appointment slot (foreign key [id_medecin]);
  • lines 29–32: the time slot, “8:00 – 8:20.” The format [%02d] of [sprintf] writes a two-digit integer at a minimum, padded with zeros: [8:05] rather than [8:5].

docs.title: 11.8.6. app/Models/Rv.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Models/Rv.php: an appointment (table [rv]): one client, in one time slot, on a
// given day.
// Uniqueness constraint SQL: unq1_rv (day, id_creneau)—a time slot is reserved
// only once per day. Created by the SQL script, identified by its name in the
// business layer.

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

class Rv extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'rv';

    public $timestamps = false;

    protected $fillable = ['jour', 'id_creneau', 'id_client'];

     // immutable_date: the column [jour] (type SQL DATE) becomes a date
     // CarbonImmutable, at midnight; it is written in the base format yyyy-mm-dd
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['jour' => 'immutable_date', 'id_creneau' => 'integer', 'id_client' => 'integer',
            'version' => 'integer'];
    }

    public function client(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Client::class, 'id_client');
    }

    public function creneau(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Creneau::class, 'id_creneau');
    }
}
  • Lines 23–27: The column [jour] (type SQL [DATE]) is converted to [CarbonImmutable], the date class of [Laravel] (example 12), at midnight. Immutable: its methods never modify the object; they return a new one ([$jour->addDay()] returns the next day, [$jour] remains unchanged). The entire application handles immutable dates: a date shared among multiple objects cannot be modified by one of them without the others’ knowledge;
  • lines 29–34: two relationships, one to the client and one to the appointment time slot.

// that may have been scheduled within this time slot on a given day (null if the time slot is available).

namespace App\Domain;

use App\Models\Creneau;
use App\Models\Rv;

readonly class CreneauMedecinJour

<?php
// app/Domain/AgendaMedecinJour.php: a doctor’s complete schedule for a given day
// given, the list of their time slots, each marked as available or booked. Calculated by
// MetierService::getAgendaMedecinJour, converted into a table HTML by

use App\Models\Medecin;

Two calculated objects that do not correspond to any table: a time slot and its potential appointment on a given day; a doctor’s calendar for a single day, listing their available time slots. These are classes of type [readonly] (example 03), whose properties are declared in the constructor. The comment [/** @param list<CreneauMedecinJour> ... */] specifies the contents of the array: [PHP] cannot determine the type of an array’s contents, but editors ([PHP Intelephense]) and analysis tools read these comments, known as [PHPDoc].

docs.title: 11.10. The DAO layer
docs.text: The DAO layer (Example 28) groups the queries: one class per table, with no business logic. Its methods do not start transactions; the business layer calls them within its own transactions. They use the query builder from [Eloquent]: [where], [orderBy], [first], [get]... ; the values in these queries become parameters for the SQL query: no SQL injection is possible.

docs.title: 11.10.1. app/Dao/PersonneDao.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Dao/PersonneDao.php: the DAO layer shared by doctors and clients.
//
// The DAO for doctors and clients would be identical: this ABSTRAITE
// writes them only once. $this->model is the relevant Eloquent class
// (Doctor::class or Client::class): $this->model::query() initiates a query
// on the SA table.
//
// Queries are written using the Eloquent query builder (where,
// orderBy...); Eloquent translates them into SQL. The values (first_name, last_name...)
// become part of the query’s PARAMÈTRES: no string concatenation, so
// no SQL injection. These methods do not open any transactions: it is the
// business layer that calls them, within its own transactions.

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Personne;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

abstract class PersonneDao
{
     /** @param class-string<Person> $modele */
    public function __construct(protected string $modele)
    {
    }

     // a query on the class table, including the user account
    protected function requete(): Builder
    {
         // with('account'): loads AUSSI the accounts via a second query
         // (SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (...)). Without it, every access to
         // $personne->account would trigger its own query
        return $this->modele::query()->with('compte');
    }

     // list sorted by last name then first name
    public function lister(): Collection
    {
        return $this->requete()->orderBy('nom')->orderBy('prenom')->get();
    }

     // a person and their account; null if they do not exist
    public function lire(int $id): ?Personne
    {
        return $this->requete()->find($id);
    }

     // the person whose user account is [$idUser]
    public function lireParUser(int $idUser): ?Personne
    {
        return $this->requete()->where('user', $idUser)->first();
    }

     // the person with these first and last names, if such a person exists. The comparison is
     // performed by MySQL, i.e., using the database’s collation (utf8mb4_unicode_ci: without
     // taking into account capital letters or accents)—exactly the same rule as
     // the one for the uniqueness constraint SQL
    public function homonyme(string $prenom, string $nom): ?Personne
    {
        return $this->modele::query()->where('prenom', $prenom)->where('nom', $nom)->first();
    }

     // INSERT: the database generates the ID, which Eloquent stores in the object
    public function ajouter(array $colonnes): Personne
    {
        return $this->modele::query()->create($colonnes);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the VERROU OPTIMISTE (see Example 28):
        // UPDATE ... SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?
     // returns the number of modified lines: 0 if the line has been modified (or
     // deleted) since it was read
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function modifier(int $id, int $version, array $colonnes): int
    {
        return $this->modele::query()->whereKey($id)->where('version', $version)
            ->update([...$colonnes, 'version' => DB::raw('version + 1')]);
    }

     // a DELETE sent directly to the database, without reading the person first
    public function supprimer(int $id): void
    {
        $this->modele::query()->whereKey($id)->delete();
    }
}

The DAO layer common to both doctors and clients, defined once in an abstract class.

  • Line 25: the relevant class [Eloquent], [Medecin::class], or [Client::class] (a string, the full name of the class). The comment [@param class-string<Personne>] clarifies this for developers. [$this->modele::query()] calls the static method [query] of this class: [PHP] accepts a variable instead of a class name. [query()] initiates a query on the model table; [Medecin::where(...)] is a shortcut for it;
  • Lines 30–36: A query that also loads the accounts of the people retrieved: [with('compte')] requests the preloading of the relation [compte]. [Eloquent] then executes two queries: one for the individuals, followed by one for all their accounts at once ([select * from users where id in (2, 3, 4)]; see the console output above). Without this, the list of doctors displayed by the administrator would trigger one query per doctor upon the first access to [$medecin->compte->login]: this is the so-called “N + 1 queries” problem. Another reason: the lists of doctors and clients are stored in the cache ([ApplicationModel], discussed later); the objects retrieved from the cache must be complete;
  • lines 39–42: the list, sorted by last name then first name; [get()] returns a [Collection] and a [Eloquent] (example 28);
  • lines 45–48: [find] reads a row by its primary key; [null] if it does not exist;
  • lines 51–54: the person whose account is [$idUser]: [first()] returns the first row, or [null];
  • lines 60–63: the person with the same first and last name. The comparison is performed using [MySQL], with the database’s collation: ignoring uppercase letters and accents, exactly as in the uniqueness constraint (example 28);
  • lines 66–69: [create] inserts a row (columns from [$fillable]) and returns the object, along with the ID generated by the database;
  • lines 77–81: the optimistic lock from Example 28: [UPDATE ... SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?]. The method returns the number of modified rows: 0 if the row has been modified or deleted since it was read. [[...$colonnes, 'version' => ...]] creates an array containing the elements of [$colonnes], plus the version (the [...] operator unpacks an array). [whereKey($id)]: the condition on the primary key;
  • lines 84–87: a [DELETE] sent directly to the database, without reading the row first.

docs.title: 11.10.2. app/Dao/MedecinDao.php and ClientDao.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Dao/MedecinDao.php: the DAO for doctors—everything is inherited from PersonneDao.

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Medecin;

class MedecinDao extends PersonneDao
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct(Medecin::class);
    }
}

Everything is inherited: the constructor only specifies the class [Eloquent] to [PersonneDao] ([parent::__construct] calls the parent class’s constructor).

<?php
// app/Dao/ClientDao.php: the DAO for clients—the one for individuals, plus a
// locking method.

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Client;

class ClientDao extends PersonneDao
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct(Client::class);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // places a VERROU on a customer’s line until the end of the transaction in
     // progress (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), and returns its ID (null if the client does
     // ). A second transaction that requests the same lock ATTEND as the
     // first one has completed.
     // Used for scheduling appointments (see MetierService::ajouterRv): two
     // simultaneous appointments for the same patient are thus processed—one
     // APRÈS the other, and the second reservation sees the appointment created by the first.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function verrouiller(int $id): ?int
    {
        return Client::query()->whereKey($id)->lockForUpdate()->value('id');
    }
}
  • Lines 25–28: a pessimistic lock, the other type of lock. [lockForUpdate()] adds [FOR UPDATE] to the query: [SELECT id FROM clients WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE]. The row being read is locked until the end of the current transaction: another transaction requesting the same lock waits for the first one to finish. [value('id')] returns the value of a column in the first row ([null] if there is none). We’ll see, in the business layer, what this lock is used for.

docs.title: 11.10.3. app/Dao/CreneauDao.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Dao/CreneauDao.php: DAO layer for time slots.

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Creneau;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;

class CreneauDao
{
     // a time slot and its doctor
    public function lire(int $id): ?Creneau
    {
        return Creneau::with('medecin')->find($id);
    }

     // a doctor’s time slots, in chronological order
    public function listerParMedecin(int $idMedecin): Collection
    {
        return Creneau::where('id_medecin', $idMedecin)->orderBy('hdebut')->orderBy('mdebut')->get();
    }

     // deletes all of a doctor’s time slots (deleting a doctor):
        // DELETE FROM time slots WHERE id_medecin = ?
    public function supprimerParMedecin(int $idMedecin): void
    {
        Creneau::where('id_medecin', $idMedecin)->delete();
    }
}

[Creneau::with('medecin')->find($id)]: a time slot and its doctor (preloaded); [Creneau::where(...)->delete()]: a [DELETE] containing all rows that satisfy the condition.

docs.title: 11.10.4. app/Dao/RvDao.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Dao/RvDao.php: DAO layer for appointments.
//
// The [rv] table does not directly reference the doctor: it goes through the appointment slot.
// whereHas('time slot', ...): appointments whose time slot meets a condition
// (Eloquent writes this as SQL with a subquery EXISTS).

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Rv;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;

class RvDao
{
     // an appointment, its client, and its time slot
    public function lire(int $id): ?Rv
    {
        return Rv::with(['client', 'creneau'])->find($id);
    }

     // a doctor’s appointments on a given day, along with their clients
    public function rvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): Collection
    {
        return Rv::with('client')
            ->where('jour', $jour->toDateString())
            ->whereHas('creneau', fn (Builder $q) => $q->where('id_medecin', $idMedecin))
            ->get();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // a client’s appointments starting from the day [$depuis] (inclusive), in chronological order
     // chronological order, with the time slot ET and the doctor for that time slot ('creneau.medecin':
     // a relation of the relation). The sort is based on columns from the table
     // [creneaux]: a JOINTURE SQL is required; select('rv.*'): only the
     // columns from [rv] to populate the Rv objects
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function rvAVenirClient(int $idClient, CarbonImmutable $depuis): Collection
    {
        return Rv::with('creneau.medecin')
            ->select('rv.*')
            ->join('creneaux', 'creneaux.id', '=', 'rv.id_creneau')
            ->where('rv.id_client', $idClient)
            ->where('rv.jour', '>=', $depuis->toDateString())
            ->orderBy('rv.jour')->orderBy('creneaux.hdebut')->orderBy('creneaux.mdebut')
            ->get();
    }

     // number of appointments for a client starting from day [$depuis] (inclusive)
    public function compterAVenirClient(int $idClient, CarbonImmutable $depuis): int
    {
        return Rv::where('id_client', $idClient)->where('jour', '>=', $depuis->toDateString())->count();
    }

     // number of appointments (past or future) for a doctor
    public function compterParMedecin(int $idMedecin): int
    {
        return Rv::whereHas('creneau', fn (Builder $q) => $q->where('id_medecin', $idMedecin))->count();
    }

    public function ajouter(CarbonImmutable $jour, int $idCreneau, int $idClient): Rv
    {
        return Rv::create(['jour' => $jour, 'id_creneau' => $idCreneau, 'id_client' => $idClient]);
    }

     // DELETE FROM rv WHERE id = ?
    public function supprimer(int $id): void
    {
        Rv::whereKey($id)->delete();
    }

     // deletes TOUS a client’s appointments (past and future)
    public function supprimerParClient(int $idClient): void
    {
        Rv::where('id_client', $idClient)->delete();
    }
}

The [rv] table does not directly reference the doctor: it goes through the time slot.

  • Lines 24–30: a doctor’s appointments on a given day. [whereHas('creneau', fonction)] retains the appointments for which the [creneau] relationship satisfies the condition defined by the function: [Eloquent] translates this into a subquery [EXISTS] (see the console output above). [fn (Builder $q) => ...] is an arrow function (example 03); it receives the query on table [creneaux]. The date is compared in its [aaaa-mm-jj] format ([toDateString()]), which is the same as that of the columns in [DATE];
  • Lines 39–48: A client’s upcoming appointments, along with their time slot and the doctor assigned to that slot: [with('creneau.medecin')] loads a relation from the relation. The sort is based on the time of the time slot, a column in table [creneaux]: a join is required ([join]). [select('rv.*')] retains only the columns from table [rv] to populate the [Rv] objects (otherwise, the slot ID would overwrite the appointment ID: both columns are named [id]);
  • lines 51–54: [count()] executes a [SELECT COUNT(*)];
  • lines 62–65: the object [CarbonImmutable] is written to the database in the column’s format, using the conversion declared by the model.

docs.title: 11.10.5. app/Dao/UserDao.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Dao/UserDao.php: DAO layer for user accounts. Create (or delete)
// A doctor or client can also create (or delete) their own account—see app/Metier.

namespace App\Dao;

use App\Models\Role;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

class UserDao
{
     // null if no user has this login
    public function lireParLogin(string $login): ?User
    {
        return User::where('login', $login)->first();
    }

    public function ajouter(string $login, string $hachage, string $nom, Role $role): User
    {
        return User::create(['login' => $login, 'password' => $hachage, 'nom' => $nom, 'role' => $role]);
    }

     // optimistic lock, like PersonneDao::modify
    public function modifier(int $id, int $version, array $colonnes): int
    {
        return User::whereKey($id)->where('version', $version)
            ->update([...$colonnes, 'version' => DB::raw('version + 1')]);
    }

    public function supprimer(int $id): void
    {
        User::whereKey($id)->delete();
    }
}

Accounts: viewing by login, adding, modifying with optimistic locking, deleting.

docs.title: 11.11. The business layer
docs.text: The business layer brings together business rules and transactions (Example 28). It is described by an interface and implemented by two classes: [MetierService], the business layer itself, and [ApplicationModel], the web layer cache (discussed later).

docs.title: 11.11.1. app/Metier/Dates.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Metier/Dates.php: today’s date. It is used for RÈGLES, DE, and GESTION (no
// past appointments; only one appointment per patient at VENIR): it resides
// in the business layer. The web layer reuses it.

namespace App\Metier;

use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;

class Dates
{
     // today at midnight, in the application’s time zone (config/app.php)
    public static function aujourdhui(): CarbonImmutable
    {
        return CarbonImmutable::today();
    }
}

The current date at midnight in the application’s time zone ([config/app.php]). It is used for business rules (no reservations in the past, only one upcoming appointment): it resides in the business layer. A static method ([static]) is called without creating an object: [Dates::aujourdhui()].

docs.title: 11.11.2. app/Metier/MetierException.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Metier/MetierException.php: the exception thrown by the business layer when a
// RÈGLE DE GESTION is violated (username already taken, doctor who still has
// appointments, time slot already reserved...). It does not carry text, but a
// CLÉ translation (e.g., "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): the web layer will
// will translate it into French or English when the page is displayed (see lang/*.json).
//
// A MetierException is not an error: it is a normal response ("this login
// is already taken”), displayed to the user. Any other exception is a true
// error, which results in a 500 error page.

namespace App\Metier;

use RuntimeException;
use Throwable;

class MetierException extends RuntimeException
{
    public function __construct(
         // message translation key
        public readonly string $cle,
         // any message parameters (:minutes...)
        public readonly array $parametres = [],
        ?Throwable $previous = null,
    ) {
        parent::__construct($cle, 0, $previous);
    }
}

The exception thrown when a business rule is violated. It does not carry text, but rather a translation key ([ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN]) and its parameters: the web layer will translate it into the page’s language (example 22). The business layer knows nothing about the interface languages. [RuntimeException] is a subclass of [PHP]. The constructor properties [public readonly] are declared and initialized by the constructor promotion (Example 03); [parent::__construct($cle, 0, $previous)] calls the constructor of [RuntimeException], passing the message, the code, and the previous exception (the one that caused this one—a database error, for example: it appears in the log along with the new one).

<?php
// app/Metier/DonneesPersonne.php: data entered in a "doctor"
// or “client” form, as transmitted by the web layer to the business layer.

namespace App\Metier;

readonly class DonneesPersonne
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $titre,        // Mr., Mrs., Ms.
        public string $nom,
        public string $prenom,
         // creation: optional (null), defaults to the name in lowercase
         // modification: optional; the login remains unchanged if omitted
        public ?string $login = null,
         // creation: optional; defaults to the login
         // modification: optional; the password remains unchanged if omitted

    ) {

Data from a “person” form, as transmitted by the web layer to the business layer: a class named [readonly]. The login, password, and version are optional ([?string], [?int], default value [null]); the comments explain what their absence means.

docs.title: 11.11.4. app/Metier/Metier.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Metier/Metier.php: the CONTRAT from the business layer: read operations, calendar,
// appointments, doctor and client management.
//
// A INTERFACE describes the methods a class must have, without specifying how
// they are written. MetierService (the business layer) and ApplicationModel (the cache
// of the web layer) both implement it; PHP checks, when loading
// the class, that no methods are missing.
//
// ?Type: a result that may be absent (null: a doctor who does not exist...).

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Models\Client;
use App\Models\Creneau;
use App\Models\Medecin;
use App\Models\Rv;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;

interface Metier
{
     // ------------------------------------------------ readings
    public function getAllClients(): Collection;

    public function getAllMedecins(): Collection;

    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): Collection;

    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): Collection;

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client;

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin;

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv;

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau;

    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour;

     // the client (patient) whose user account is [$idUser]
    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client;

     // a client’s appointments, for today or in the future, with time slot and doctor
    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): Collection;

     // ------------------------------------------------ appointments (ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER)
     // generates a MetierException if:
       // - the day has passed ("ERRORS.PAST_DATE");
       // - the patient already has an upcoming appointment ("ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT");
       // - the time slot is already booked for that day ("ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED").
    public function ajouterRv(CarbonImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv;

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void;

     // ------------------------------------------------ doctors (ADMIN)
     // creates a user account for the doctor ET (role DOCTOR)
    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin;

     // modifies the doctor ET's user account
    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin;

     // deletes the doctor, his time slots, and his account (ET) — rejected if he has appointments
    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void;

     // ------------------------------------------------ clients
     // (ADMIN; ajouterClient is also used to register a patient,
     // modifierClient and supprimerClient for the patient to create their own account)
     //creates the client ET and their user account (role USER)
    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client;

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client;

     // deletes the client, their account ET, and all their appointments (past and future)
    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void;
}

The business layer contract: an interface (example 06), the list of methods, without their code. Read operations return [Eloquent] or [Collection] objects; [?Client]: a client, or [null] if it does not exist. The comments specify the rules for each write operation and the keys of the [MetierException] objects it may create.

docs.title: 11.11.5. app/Metier/Descripteur.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Metier/Descripteur.php: everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client for the
// management rules (see MetierService). Doctors and clients follow the
// same rules: the common code is written UNE times and configured by a descriptor.

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Dao\PersonneDao;
use App\Models\Role;
use Closure;

readonly class Descripteur
{
    public function __construct(
        public PersonneDao $dao,
        public Role $role,              // DOCTOR or USER
        public string $cleIntrouvable,  // message if the person does not exist
        public string $cleExisteDeja,   // message if the same first and last names already exist
         // optional (null): if present, the deletion is REFUSÉE as long as the
         // person has appointments (compterRv(id) > 0), with the message cleAvecRv
        public ?Closure $compterRv,
        public ?string $cleAvecRv,
         // optional: what to delete for the person (the rows that
         // via a foreign key); receives their ID
        public ?Closure $avantSuppression,
    ) {
    }
}

Doctors and clients follow the same management rules, with a few minor differences: the DAO, the account role, error messages, and the deletion rule. This descriptor brings these details together; the common code reads them. Two properties are functions ([?Closure]: a function, or [null]): the appointment count, which prevents deletion (doctors only), and the deletion of what references the person.

docs.title: 11.11.6. app/Metier/MetierService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Metier/MetierService.php: the business layer implementation.
//
// The management of doctors and clients follows three business rules:
//
//    1. A person (doctor or client) and their user account are TOUJOURS
//       as a pair: they are created, modified, and deleted together, within the same
//       TRANSACTION—either everything succeeds, or nothing is written;
//    2. The login is unique throughout the application, and two doctors (or two
//       customers) cannot have the same first and last names;
//    3. Deletion:
//       - A MÉDECIN with appointments cannot be deleted (their patients
//         would lose their appointments without being notified): you must first
//         canceled first. Its time slots disappear along with it;
//       - a CLIENT, on the other hand, disappears along with TOUS its appointments (past and future) -
//         whether the deletion comes from the ADMIN or the patient themselves.
//
// And two rules for scheduling appointments, regardless of the role of the person
// making the appointment (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient themselves):
//    4. No appointments in the past;
//    5. A patient can have only one upcoming appointment at a time.
//
// Doctors and patients follow exactly the same rules: the common code is
// is written UNE times (private methods xxxPersonne), and configured by a descriptor
// that specifies what type of person is involved.
//
// The TRANSACTIONS files are opened using the transaction method (end-of-file),
// which also translates errors reported by the database into MetierException.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Dao\ClientDao;
use App\Dao\CreneauDao;
use App\Dao\MedecinDao;
use App\Dao\RvDao;
use App\Dao\UserDao;
use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Domain\CreneauMedecinJour;
use App\Models\Client;
use App\Models\Creneau;
use App\Models\Medecin;
use App\Models\Personne;
use App\Models\Role;
use App\Models\Rv;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Database\QueryException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class MetierService implements Metier
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Database errors -> MetierException
    //
     // When a constraint UNIQUE rejects a write operation, Laravel raises a
     // QueryException, whose message is that of MySQL. It references the NOM from the
     //constraint:
        // Duplicate entry 'Marie-PELISSIER' for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'
     // (MySQL prefixes the name with the table name, MariaDB does not). That is why
     // that the script SQL NOMME has all its constraints.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private const MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES = [
        'unq_users_login' => 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN',
        'unq_medecins_prenom_nom' => 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
        'unq_clients_prenom_nom' => 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
        'unq1_rv' => 'ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED',
    ];

    private const CONTRAINTE = "/for key '(?:[^'.]*\\.)?([^']+)'/";

    private Descripteur $medecin;

    private Descripteur $client;

     // all dependencies are provided by the Laravel service container
     // (dependency injection; see Example 06)
    public function __construct(
        private MedecinDao $medecins,
        private ClientDao $clients,
        private CreneauDao $creneaux,
        private RvDao $rvs,
        private UserDao $users,
    ) {
        $this->medecin = new Descripteur(
            dao: $medecins,
            role: Role::DOCTOR,
            cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND',
            cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
             // $rvs->compterParMedecin(...): the method itself, as a closure
             // (so-called “first-class callable” syntax)
            compterRv: $rvs->compterParMedecin(...),
            cleAvecRv: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS',
             // A walk-in clinic may still have time slots:
             // they no longer make sense without it, so they are removed along with it (otherwise the
             // foreign key creneaux.id_medecin would prevent the deletion)
            avantSuppression: $creneaux->supprimerParMedecin(...));

        $this->client = new Descripteur(
            dao: $clients,
            role: Role::USER,
            cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND',
            cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
             // no compterRv: deleting a client is never denied;
             // their appointments (past and future) are deleted along with them (otherwise
             // (the foreign key rv.id_client would prevent deletion)
            compterRv: null,
            cleAvecRv: null,
            avantSuppression: $rvs->supprimerParClient(...));
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // appointments
    // =======================================================================

    public function getAllClients(): Collection
    {
        return $this->clients->lister();
    }

    public function getAllMedecins(): Collection
    {
        return $this->medecins->lister();
    }

    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): Collection
    {
        return $this->creneaux->listerParMedecin($idMedecin);
    }

    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): Collection
    {
        return $this->rvs->rvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client
    {
        return $this->clients->lire($id);
    }

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin
    {
        return $this->medecins->lire($id);
    }

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv
    {
        return $this->rvs->lire($id);
    }

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau
    {
        return $this->creneaux->lire($id);
    }

    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client
    {
        return $this->clients->lireParUser($idUser);
    }

    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): Collection
    {
        return $this->rvs->rvAVenirClient($idClient, Dates::aujourdhui());
    }

     // a doctor’s schedule for a given day: their time slots, and for each one, the
     // appointment scheduled for that day (null if the slot is free)
    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour
    {
        $medecin = $this->getMedecinById($idMedecin);
        if ($medecin === null) {
            return null;
        }
         // slot number -> appointment scheduled for that slot (keyBy: a collection
         // indexed by the value of a column)
        $reservations = $this->getRvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour)->keyBy('id_creneau');
        $creneauxMedecinJour = $this->getAllCreneaux($idMedecin)
            ->map(fn (Creneau $creneau) => new CreneauMedecinJour($creneau, $reservations->get($creneau->id)))
            ->all();
        return new AgendaMedecinJour($medecin, $jour, $creneauxMedecinJour);
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // appointment
    // =======================================================================

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // appointment scheduling, within a transaction:
        // 1. no past appointments;
        // 2. on the patient’s line (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): if the same
           // patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs, double
           // click...), the second transaction waits for the first one to finish—and sees
           // the appointment it has just created;
        // 3. only one upcoming appointment per patient;
        // 4. Finally, the insertion. If the time slot has just been booked by a AUTRE patient,
           // it is the constraint SQL unq1_rv (day, id_creneau) that rejects
           // the insertion—translated to MetierException by transaction().
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function ajouterRv(CarbonImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv
    {
        return $this->transaction(function () use ($jour, $creneau, $client) {
            $aujourdhui = Dates::aujourdhui();
            if ($jour->lt($aujourdhui)) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PAST_DATE');
            }
            $idPatient = $this->clients->verrouiller($client->id)
                ?? throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
            if ($this->rvs->compterAVenirClient($idPatient, $aujourdhui) > 0) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT');
            }
            return $this->rvs->ajouter($jour, $creneau->id, $idPatient);
        });
    }

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void
    {
        $this->transaction(fn () => $this->rvs->supprimer($rv->id));
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // doctors and clients—public methods delegate to
     // shared private methods, with the correct descriptor
    // =======================================================================

    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return $this->ajouterPersonne($this->medecin, $donnees);
    }

    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return $this->modifierPersonne($this->medecin, $id, $donnees);
    }

    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void
    {
        $this->supprimerPersonne($this->medecin, $id);
    }

    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return $this->ajouterPersonne($this->client, $donnees);
    }

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return $this->modifierPersonne($this->client, $id, $donnees);
    }

     // the client, their account ET all their appointments (ADMIN, or the patient themselves
     // from “Manage My Account”: same method, same rule)
    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void
    {
        $this->supprimerPersonne($this->client, $id);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // creation: the user account, PUIS the person (who references it), in
     // UNE transaction.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function ajouterPersonne(Descripteur $d, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne
    {
        $nom = Str::upper(trim($donnees->nom));
        $prenom = trim($donnees->prenom);
         // Rules for the dbrdvmedecins2 database: login = name in lowercase, password
         // password = login—unless the ADMIN (or the patient) has entered others
        $login = Str::lower($donnees->login ?: $nom);
        $password = $donnees->password ?: $login;

        return $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $donnees, $nom, $prenom, $login, $password) {
            $this->verifierPersonneUnique($d, $prenom, $nom, null);
            $this->verifierLoginLibre($login);
             // Hash::make: the bcrypt hash of the password (see config/hashing.php)
            $user = $this->users->ajouter($login, Hash::make($password), "$prenom $nom", $d->role);
            $personne = $d->dao->ajouter(['titre' => $donnees->titre, 'nom' => $nom,
                'prenom' => $prenom, 'user' => $user->id]);
             // setRelation: the account, already in memory, is stored in the relation
             // [compte] for the person (no need to read it again from the database)
            return $personne->setRelation('compte', $user);
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // modification: the person ET modifies their account (the displayed name "first name NOM" must
     // match; the username and password only change if they were entered).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function modifierPersonne(Descripteur $d, int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne
    {
        return $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $id, $donnees) {
            $personne = $d->dao->lire($id) ?? throw new MetierException($d->cleIntrouvable);

             // optimistic lock: if the version in the database is no longer the same as the
             // form, someone has modified this record in the meantime—the operation is rejected
             // rather than silently overwriting the person’s changes
            $version = $donnees->version ?? $personne->version;
            if ($version !== $personne->version) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
            }

            $nom = Str::upper(trim($donnees->nom));
            $prenom = trim($donnees->prenom);
            $this->verifierPersonneUnique($d, $prenom, $nom, $id);

             // the person: UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND version = ? (if the record has
             // been modified; APRÈS as shown above, no rows are modified)
            if ($d->dao->modifier($id, $version, ['titre' => $donnees->titre, 'nom' => $nom,
                'prenom' => $prenom]) === 0) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
            }

             // their account: the displayed name, and, if entered, the login and
             // password
            $compte = $personne->compte;
            $colonnes = ['nom' => "$prenom $nom"];
            $login = $donnees->login ? Str::lower($donnees->login) : null;
            if ($login !== null && $login !== $compte->login) {
                $this->verifierLoginLibre($login);
                $colonnes['login'] = $login;
            }
            if ($donnees->password) {
                $colonnes['password'] = Hash::make($donnees->password);
            }
            if ($this->users->modifier($compte->id, $compte->version, $colonnes) === 0) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
            }

             // the person re-read: their new values, their new versions
            return $d->dao->lire($id);
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // deletion, in transaction UNE, in the order dictated by the keys
     // foreign keys:
        // 1. possible rejection if there are remaining appointments (with a doctor);
        // 2. information identifying the person (doctor’s time slots, patient’s
           // client);
        // 3. the person (who references their account);
        // 4. their account.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function supprimerPersonne(Descripteur $d, int $id): void
    {
        $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $id) {
            $personne = $d->dao->lire($id) ?? throw new MetierException($d->cleIntrouvable);
            if ($d->compterRv !== null && ($d->compterRv)($id) > 0) {
                throw new MetierException($d->cleAvecRv);
            }
            if ($d->avantSuppression !== null) {
                ($d->avantSuppression)($id);
            }
            $d->dao->supprimer($id);
            $this->users->supprimer($personne->user);
        });
    }

     // Rejects first and last names already used by a AUTRE person of the same type
     // ($idCourant: the person being edited, who obviously has the right
     // to keep their own first and last names; null for a new record)
    private function verifierPersonneUnique(Descripteur $d, string $prenom, string $nom, ?int $idCourant): void
    {
        $homonyme = $d->dao->homonyme($prenom, $nom);
        if ($homonyme !== null && $homonyme->id !== $idCourant) {
            throw new MetierException($d->cleExisteDeja);
        }
    }

    private function verifierLoginLibre(string $login): void
    {
        if ($this->users->lireParLogin($login) !== null) {
            throw new MetierException('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN');
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // executes [$travail] within a transaction (DB::transaction, see Example 28):
     // COMMIT if the function terminates normally; if an exception occurs
     // (including MetierException), ROLLBACK: nothing is written.
    //
     // The "free login" and "unique first name + last name" checks are performed AVANT
     // the entry, to provide a clear message. But two ADMIN entries could
     // register the same login (or the same doctor) at the same time: in this case
     // — though rare — a uniqueness constraint SQL prevents the second write. It
     // therefore intercepts errors from the transaction’s database AUTOUR, to
     // translate them into the same MetierException. Any other error is a true
     // anomaly: it is allowed to be reported.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function transaction(Closure $travail): mixed
    {
        try {
            return DB::transaction($travail);
        } catch (QueryException $e) {
            if (preg_match(self::CONTRAINTE, $e->getMessage(), $m)
                && isset(self::MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES[$m[1]])) {
                throw new MetierException(self::MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES[$m[1]], previous: $e);
            }
            throw $e;
        }
    }
}

The most important file in the application. We’ll go through it by topic.

docs.title: 11.11.6.1. The descriptors
docs.text: Lines 89–113: the two descriptors, created once by the constructor. The named arguments ([dao: $medecins], example 01) make the call readable. [$rvs->compterParMedecin(...)] (with three dots in parentheses) does not count anything: it is the syntax of [PHP] 8.1 that generates, from a method, a [Closure]—a function that will be called later ([($d->compterRv)($id)], line 349). A doctor is removed along with their time slots ([supprimerParMedecin]), but not if they have appointments; a client is removed along with all their appointments ([supprimerParClient]).

docs.title: 11.11.6.2. Readings and the calendar
docs.text: The readings (lines 120–165) are delegated to the DAO layer. A doctor’s schedule (lines 172–185) is calculated: the doctor, their time slots, and the appointments for that day. [keyBy('id_creneau')] transforms the collection of appointments into a collection indexed by slot number: [$reservations->get($creneau->id)] returns the appointment for a given slot, or [null]. [map] transforms each time slot into [CreneauMedecinJour]; [all()] returns the array [PHP] contained in the collection.

docs.title: 11.11.6.3. Scheduling an Appointment
docs.text:
Lines 203–217: four steps, in a single transaction.

  • No past appointments: [$jour->lt($aujourdhui)] (*less than*) compares two dates;
  • the patient’s record is locked ([verrouiller], [SELECT ... FOR UPDATE]). Why? The rule “only one upcoming appointment per patient” is verified by a count (third step), then the insertion takes place (fourth step). If the same patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs, a double-click), both transactions could count zero appointments and then each insert its own: the rule would be violated. With the lock, the second transaction waits for the first one to finish, then counts... one appointment. [?? throw new MetierException(...)]: if the client no longer exists, [verrouiller] returns [null], and the operator [??] evaluates its second operand, which raises the exception (since [PHP] 8, [throw] is an expression);
  • counting upcoming appointments;
  • insertion. If the time slot has just been taken by another patient, the database constraint [unq1_rv] rejects the insertion: the method [transaction] translates this error into [MetierException].

docs.title: 11.11.6.4. Managing Doctors and Clients
docs.text:
The public methods (lines 229–256) call the shared private methods, using the correct descriptor.

  • Lines 265–285: creation. The last name is capitalized ([Str::upper]), and the first name and last name have unnecessary spaces removed ([trim]). By default, the login is the last name in lowercase, and the password is the login (as per the rules for demo accounts): [$a ?: $b] is equivalent to [$a] if it is “valid” (neither [null] nor an empty string), and [$b] otherwise. In the transaction: the validations (first and last names can be any value, login can be any value), followed by the account, hashed as [Hash::make] (example 25), followed by the person, who references the account. [setRelation('compte', $user)] stores the account—already in memory—in the person’s record: [$personne->compte] will not trigger a query. [use (...)]: an ordinary anonymous function ([function () use ($d, ...)]) cannot see the variables of the method that contains it; [use] passes them to it (an arrow function, [fn () =>], sees them on its own, but can only contain an expression);
  • Lines 291–334: the modification, with two optimistic locks. The first is a comparison: the form’s version (hidden field, Example 28) must match that of the record in the database; otherwise, someone modified the record between the time the form was displayed and the time it was submitted. The second is the [WHERE version = ?] clause of the [UPDATE] ([PersonneDao::modifier]), which detects a change that occurred between reading and writing. The account is processed as follows: its displayed name (“first name NOM”) is always updated; its login and password are updated only if they were entered; its own optimistic lock also protects the row in the [users] table. The person is finally read again: the caller receives their new values and new versions;
  • lines 345–358: deletion, in the order dictated by the foreign keys: first what references the person (time slots or appointments), then the person, then their account. The reverse order would be rejected by the database: a row that is still referenced by a foreign key cannot be deleted;
  • lines 363–369: the person being modified is allowed to retain their own first and last names; [$idCourant] is equivalent to [null] for a new record.

docs.title: 11.11.6.5. Transactions and uniqueness constraints
docs.text:
Lines 391–402: All postings go through this method. [DB::transaction] executes the function in a transaction (Example 28): [COMMIT] if it completes normally, [ROLLBACK] if an exception occurs—including [MetierException]: a rule violation in the middle of an operation leaves no trace. The “login available” and “first and last names available” checks are performed before writing to the database, to provide a clear message. However, two administrators could attempt to register the same login at the same time: each finds it available, and the second [INSERT] is rejected by the constraint [unq_users_login]. [Laravel] then raises a [QueryException], whose message is that of [MySQL]; it contains the name of the violated constraint:

SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry 'dupont' for key 'unq_users_login'

The regular expression on line 74 extracts this name ([MySQL] 8 prefixes it with the table name, [users.unq_users_login], but [MariaDB] does not: the "[(?:[^'.]*\.)?]" part accepts both forms), and the array in lines 67–72 provides the message key. Any other database error is a true anomaly: it is retried ([throw $e]) and will result in a 500 error page.

docs.title: 11.12. Authentication
docs.text: The [app/Auth] file includes examples 25 through 27, featuring database users and a few additional security measures.

docs.title: 11.12.1. app/Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.php: the logged-in user, as described by their
// token JWT (see Example 25). Authenticatable: the interface that Laravel expects from
// authenticated users (Auth::user(), auth()->user(), @auth in a view...).
//
// The claims in our tokens (see AuthService::cookieJeton):
//    su  b : the user account ID (convention JWT: "subject"), as plain text
//    login: the login
//    na  me: the display name ("Marie PELISSIER"), for the navigation bar
//    rol e: ADMIN, DOCTOR, or USER
//    iat, exp: token creation and expiration dates
//
// This object does not come from the database: it is reconstructed with each request at
// based on the token, whose signature guarantees its content.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Auth;

use App\Models\Role;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;

readonly class UtilisateurConnecte implements Authenticatable
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $userId,
        public string $login,
        public string $nom,
