        public Role $role,
    ) {
    }

     // the user described by the claims of an already verified token; null if a claim
     // is missing or does not have the expected format. Role::tryFrom: null for an unknown role
    public static function de(array $claims): ?self
    {
        $role = Role::tryFrom((string) ($claims['role'] ?? ''));
        if (! isset($claims['sub'], $claims['login'], $claims['nom']) || $role === null
            || ! ctype_digit((string) $claims['sub'])) {
            return null;
        }
        return new self((int) $claims['sub'], (string) $claims['login'], (string) $claims['nom'], $role);
    }

    public function estAdmin(): bool
    {
        return $this->role === Role::ADMIN;
    }

    public function estPatient(): bool
    {
        return $this->role === Role::USER;
    }

     // ---- the Authenticatable interface: the user’s identifier is the ID
     // of their account; the password and the "remember me" token from Laravel sessions
     // are irrelevant here
    public function getAuthIdentifierName(): string
    {
        return 'userId';
    }

    public function getAuthIdentifier(): int
    {
        return $this->userId;
    }

    public function getAuthPasswordName(): string
    {
        return '';
    }

    public function getAuthPassword(): string
    {
        return '';
    }

    public function getRememberToken(): ?string
    {
        return null;
    }

    public function setRememberToken($valeur): void
    {
    }

    public function getRememberTokenName(): string
    {
        return '';
    }
}

The logged-in user, as described by their token: their account ID, username, name, and role. Like [Utilisateur] in Example 25, it implements the [Authenticatable] interface, which [Laravel] expects from authenticated users. This object does not come from the database: it is reconstructed for each request based on the token, whose signature guarantees its content. The application therefore does not read the account from the database for each request.

  • Lines 35–43: The user is described by the claims in an already verified token, or [null] if one of the claims is missing or does not have the expected format. A properly signed token should never be malformed; however, the secret key could be shared with another application, which might generate different tokens: it costs nothing to be cautious. [Role::tryFrom] returns the role, or [null] for an unknown value; [ctype_digit] verifies that a string consists only of digits;
  • lines 45–50: two questions that views and controllers often ask;
  • lines 58–61 and following: the [Authenticatable] interface. The user’s identifier is their account ID; the password and the “remember me” token are irrelevant.

docs.title: 11.12.2. app/Auth/AuthService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Auth/AuthService.php: the authentication logic:
//    - validate       () : verifies a username/password pair;
//    - cookieJeton(   ) : generates the JWT token for a validated user, and the
//                         cookie that carries it;
//    - user() :    the user described by a token.
//
// Where does the JWT token travel? In a COOKIE (see Example 25): a browser
// that displays ordinary HTML pages presents it on its own, with every
// request. The settings in this cookie are important for security:
//    - HttpOnly: the page’s JavaScript cannot read the cookie (an injected script
//      could not steal the token);
//    - SameSite=Lax: the browser does not send the cookie with a PAS value originating from a
//      another site (first line of defense against the so-called CSRF attack; the second is
//      the anti-CSRF token for forms, see @csrf);
//    - Secure: in production (HTTPS), the cookie is never transmitted in plain text;
//    - Lifetime: the cookie is deleted when the token expires.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Auth;

use App\Dao\UserDao;
use App\Models\User;
use Firebase\JWT\JWT;
use Firebase\JWT\Key;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use RuntimeException;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;
use Throwable;

class AuthService
{
     // the name of the cookie that carries the token
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_jwt';

    private string $secret;

    private int $duree;

    public function __construct(private UserDao $users)
    {
        $this->secret = config('rdvmedecins.jwt.secret');
        $this->duree = config('rdvmedecins.jwt.duree');
         // HMAC-SHA256 requires a key of at least 256 bits: this is clearly stated,
         // rather than letting the library fail later
        if (strlen($this->secret) < 32) {
            throw new RuntimeException('JWT_SECRET doit comporter au moins 32 caractères (cf. .env).');
        }
    }

     // null if the login does not exist or if the password is incorrect. Hash::check
     // hashes the entered password with the "salt" contained in the stored hash,
     // then compares the two results
    public function valider(string $login, string $password): ?User
    {
        $user = $this->users->lireParLogin($login);
        if ($user === null || ! Hash::check($password, $user->password)) {
            return null;
        }
        return $user;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the token JWT from [$user], in the cookie that carries it. The token is SIGNÉ
     // (HMAC-SHA256) using the secret key: the browser can read it (it is not
     // encrypted), but it cannot modify it—any modification would render the signature
     // invalid.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function cookieJeton(User $user): Cookie
    {
        $maintenant = time();
        $claims = [
            'sub' => (string) $user->id,
            'login' => $user->login,
            'nom' => $user->nom,
            'role' => $user->role->value,
            'iat' => $maintenant,
            'exp' => $maintenant + $this->duree * 60,
        ];
        $jeton = JWT::encode($claims, $this->secret, 'HS256');
         // cookie(name, value, duration in minutes, path, domain, secure, httpOnly,
         // raw, sameSite): the Laravel function that creates a cookie
        return cookie(self::COOKIE, $jeton, $this->duree, '/', null,
            config('rdvmedecins.cookie_secure'), true, false, 'lax');
    }

     // the cookie that corresponds to EFFACE the token: same name, empty, already expired
    public static function cookieEffacement(): Cookie
    {
        return cookie()->forget(self::COOKIE);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the user identified by a token; null if the token is expired, forged, or
     // malformed. JWT::decode verifies the signature ET and the expiration date (claim exp).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function utilisateur(string $jeton): ?UtilisateurConnecte
    {
        try {
             // decode returns an object; (array) converts it to an associative array
            $claims = (array) JWT::decode($jeton, new Key($this->secret, 'HS256'));
        } catch (Throwable) {
            return null;
        }
        return UtilisateurConnecte::de($claims);
    }
}
  • Line 35: the name of the token cookie, a class constant, read by [AuthService::COOKIE]. Why not configure [config/rdvmedecins.php], like the secret key? Because [bootstrap/app.php] needs it to exclude the cookie from encryption at a time when the configuration has not yet been loaded: the code for [withMiddleware] runs before [Laravel] has read the files in the [config] folder;
  • lines 41–50: the token key and lifetime, read from the configuration. If the key is too short, this is flagged as soon as the service is created, with a clear message (see “Common Issues”);
  • lines 55–62: verification of a username and password (example 25), with the account retrieved from the database by the DAO layer. Note that this service uses the DAO layer directly, without going through the business layer: password verification is not a business rule;
  • Lines 70–86: the user’s token and the cookie that carries it. The statements are the same as in Example 25, including the account ID ([sub], a string, as required by the standard) and the username. The function [cookie] of [Laravel] generates a cookie: name, value, lifetime in minutes (that of the token), path, domain ([null]: that of the site), [secure] (in production, on HTTPS), [httpOnly], [raw] ([false]: the value is encoded for a URL) and [sameSite];
  • lines 89–92: The cookie that clears the token: [cookie()->forget(nom)] creates an empty cookie with the same name that has already expired;
  • lines 98–107: token verification (example 25).

docs.title: 11.12.3. app/Auth/SessionInvalide.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Auth/SessionInvalide.php: the token is valid, but the account it refers to
// no longer exists: it was deleted since the login (either by the patient themselves
// in another tab, or by the ADMIN). This case is treated as an expired session
// expired session: bootstrap/app.php clears the cookie and redirects to the login page.

namespace App\Auth;

use RuntimeException;

class SessionInvalide extends RuntimeException
{
}

A scenario not covered in Example 25: the token is valid, but the account it refers to no longer exists. A patient has deleted their account in one tab, but the token is still present in another tab; or the administrator has deleted the account of a logged-in patient. The token’s signature provides no indication of the account’s existence; it is only when the application searches for the patient associated with the account ([Outils::patientConnecte], discussed later) that it discovers the account no longer exists. It then throws this exception, which [bootstrap/app.php] treats as an expired session. The class is empty: only its type matters, which allows it to be associated with its own rendering function.

docs.title: 11.12.4. app/Auth/CaptchaService.php, Captcha.php, and DessinCaptcha.php
docs.text:
[DessinCaptcha.php] and [Captcha.php] are from Example 27. The service is almost the same:

<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Auth/CaptchaService.php: a CAPTCHA ("test to distinguish a human from a
// robot") generated by the server itself, without an external service (see Example 27).
//
// How it works:
//    1. `generer()` generates a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the correct
//       response DANS LE CACHE from the server under a random identifier;
//    2. The page displays the image and places the identifier in a hidden field on the
//       form (the response itself never leaves the server);
//    3. verify(id, input) compares the input to the expected response, then OUBLIE
//       this CAPTCHA: each image is used only once, so a bot cannot replay
//       a response that has already been found.
//
// Why the cache? An application PHP does not keep RIEN in memory from one request to
// the next: each request starts from scratch. Anything that needs to persist beyond a single request
// is therefore stored in the cache (in this case, files; see CACHE_STORE in .env), shared by
// all requests, and even across multiple servers using a cache like Redis.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Auth;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class CaptchaService
{
     // image validity period, in seconds: 10 minutes to fill out the form
    private const DUREE_VIE = 600;

    public function generer(): Captcha
    {
        $texte = DessinCaptcha::texteAleatoire(5);    // 5 characters
        $id = Str::random(24);                        // an unguessable identifier
         // the cache will automatically forget the answer after 10 minutes
        Cache::put("captcha:$id", $texte, self::DUREE_VIE);
        return new Captcha($id, DessinCaptcha::svg($texte));
    }

     // true if [$saisie] is the correct answer to the captcha [$id] (regardless of
     // case). The CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases.
    public function verifier(?string $id, ?string $saisie): bool
    {
        if (! $id || $saisie === null) {
            return false;
        }
        $attendu = Cache::get("captcha:$id");
         // "forget" returns true only for the request that removed the entry:
         // if two requests have the same captcha at the same time, only one
         // removes it—the other fails
        if ($attendu === null || ! Cache::forget("captcha:$id")) {
            return false;
        }
        return strcasecmp($attendu, trim($saisie)) === 0;
    }
}
  • lines 31–38: a 5-character string generated at random, a random identifier ([Str::random], which uses a cryptographic generator), and the correct answer stored in the cache for 10 minutes (Example 27);
  • lines 42–55: a difference from Example 27, which used [Cache::pull] (read, then remove). Between reading and removal, a second request displaying the same CAPTCHA could also read it: two attempts for a single solved image. Here, the answer is read, then removed by [Cache::forget], which returns [true] only if it has actually removed the entry: with file caching, this involves deleting a file, which the operating system allows only one of the two processes to do. The request that loses the race fails. This is equivalent to the lock in version [Flask], where the CAPTCHAs were kept in memory.

docs.title: 11.12.5. app/Auth/LimiteurTentatives.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Auth/LimiteurTentatives.php: second line of defense against bots (the first is
// the CAPTCHA): we track attempts, and once a threshold is exceeded, we block access for a
// time (see Example 27).
//
//    - login: after LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or incorrect
//      password) for the same login from the same IP address IP, this pair is
//      blocked until the end of a LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES-minute window, counted
//      from the first failed attempt. The same IP address IP is also blocked if it accumulates
//      5 times as many failed attempts across all logins (a bot attempting thousands
//      different login attempts);
//    - account creation: no more than INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE accounts created per
//      per hour from the same IP address IP.
//
// Caution in the classroom: all computers frequently connect to the Internet via the
// MÊME address IP. This is why the connection block first targets the
// pair (IP, login)—a student who enters the wrong password does not block their
// neighbors—and why the thresholds are adjustable (in the .env file).
//
// The counters are those of the Laravel limiter (RateLimiter), stored in the cache.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Auth;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\RateLimiter;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class LimiteurTentatives
{
    private int $maxEchecs;

    private int $blocage;    // in seconds

    private int $maxInscriptions;

    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->maxEchecs = config('rdvmedecins.login_max_echecs');
        $this->blocage = config('rdvmedecins.login_blocage_minutes') * 60;
        $this->maxInscriptions = config('rdvmedecins.inscription_max_par_heure');
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- connection

     // number of remaining minutes of lockout (0 = attempt is allowed)
    public function minutesBlocageLogin(string $ip, string $login): int
    {
        return max($this->minutesRestantes(self::cleLogin($ip, $login), $this->maxEchecs),
            $this->minutesRestantes(self::cleIp($ip), $this->maxEchecs * 5));
    }

     // RateLimiter::hit: +1 to the counter; the first hit opens a window of
     // [$this->blocage] seconds, at the end of which the counter resets to zero
    public function echecLogin(string $ip, string $login): void
    {
        RateLimiter::hit(self::cleLogin($ip, $login), $this->blocage);
        RateLimiter::hit(self::cleIp($ip), $this->blocage);
    }

     // A successful connection resets the login counter to zero
    public function reussiteLogin(string $ip, string $login): void
    {
        RateLimiter::clear(self::cleLogin($ip, $login));
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

    public function minutesBlocageInscription(string $ip): int
    {
        return $this->minutesRestantes("inscription|$ip", $this->maxInscriptions);
    }

     // one-hour window
    public function inscriptionReussie(string $ip): void
    {
        RateLimiter::hit("inscription|$ip", 3600);
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- common mechanism

     // tooManyAttempts: Has the counter reached [$maximum] within the window in
     // current window? availableIn: Seconds remaining until the end of this window,
     // rounded to the nearest minute SUPÉRIEURE: 30 seconds remaining -> "1 minute"
    private function minutesRestantes(string $cle, int $maximum): int
    {
        if (! RateLimiter::tooManyAttempts($cle, $maximum)) {
            return 0;
        }
        return max(1, (int) ceil(RateLimiter::availableIn($cle) / 60));
    }

    private static function cleLogin(string $ip, string $login): string
    {
        return "login|$ip|".Str::lower(trim($login));
    }

    private static function cleIp(string $ip): string
    {
        return "ip|$ip";
    }
}

The second line of defense against bots, after the CAPTCHA: we count the attempts, and once a threshold is exceeded, we block access. Example 27 presented the limiter from [Laravel], the facade from [RateLimiter]. This class uses it for two rules:

  • login (lines 47–62): each failed attempt (incorrect CAPTCHA or password) is counted twice—once for the pair (address IP, login), and once for the address IP alone. The pair is blocked after 5 failed attempts (setting [LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS]), and the address IP after 25, across all logins: this is the bot trying thousands of different logins. Why not block the address IP first? In a classroom (or at a company), all machines often access the Internet through the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password shouldn’t block their neighbors. [RateLimiter::hit(clé, durée)] increments the counter by 1; the first [hit] opens a 15-minute window (setting [LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES]), at the end of which the counter resets to zero. A successful login resets the counter for that user ([RateLimiter::clear]);
  • account creation (lines 69–75): a maximum of 10 accounts per hour per address IP (setting [INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE]);
  • lines 85–91: [tooManyAttempts(clé, maximum)] indicates whether the counter has reached the maximum in the current window; [availableIn(clé)] returns the number of seconds remaining in this window, rounded up to the nearest minute ([ceil]): There are 30 seconds remaining, but “1 minute” is announced. The displayed message depends on this: “Too many failed attempts. Please try again in 15 minute(s).” ;
  • lines 93–96: the counter keys. The login is converted to lowercase: [Admin] and [admin] are considered the same (as with the database; see its collation).

The counters for [RateLimiter] are stored in the cache: they are shared by all requests and survive a server restart. The command [php artisan cache:clear] clears the cache, thereby resetting all counters to zero (useful during development when you’ve gotten yourself stuck).

docs.title: 11.12.6. app/Auth/PasseInscription.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Auth/PasseInscription.php: the "pass" for account creation.
//
// To open the “Create a Customer Account” page, you must first have copied the
// captcha from the authentication page (see InscriptionController, POST
// /registration/access). The server then issues a token:
//    - a random identifier, stored in a cookie named HttpOnly;
//    - valid for 15 minutes (enough time to fill out the form, even if you have to
//      several times after data entry errors);
//    - Expires as soon as an account is created: UN captcha solved = UN account at most.
//      A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
//
// Without a valid passcode, GET and POST /registration redirect to the
// authentication page (VerifierPasseInscription middleware): type directly
// The URL /registration does not allow you to bypass the CAPTCHA.
//
// Like CAPTCHAs, passcodes are stored in the cache.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Auth;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;

class PasseInscription
{
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_inscription';

     // Pass lifetime, in minutes
    private const DUREE_VIE = 15;

     // Issues a new pass; returns its ID
    public function emettre(): string
    {
        $id = Str::random(24);
        Cache::put("passe:$id", true, self::DUREE_VIE * 60);
        return $id;
    }

     // true if [$id] is an existing, unexpired token
    public function estValide(?string $id): bool
    {
        return $id !== null && $id !== '' && Cache::has("passe:$id");
    }

     // The pass has been used: it is discarded
    public function consommer(?string $id): void
    {
        if ($id) {
            Cache::forget("passe:$id");
        }
    }

     // the cookie is sent by the browser only to addresses ending in /registration...
    public static function cookie(string $id): Cookie
    {
        return cookie(self::COOKIE, $id, self::DUREE_VIE, '/inscription', null,
            config('rdvmedecins.cookie_secure'), true, false, 'lax');
    }

     // ... and is deleted by a cookie with the same name and path that has already expired
    public static function cookieEffacement(): Cookie
    {
        return cookie()->forget(self::COOKIE, '/inscription');
    }
}

Creating a customer account is protected by the CAPTCHA on the login page. But the account creation form is on a different page ([/inscription]): how can we tell, when the form is requested, that the CAPTCHA was solved just before? Through a token: when the CAPTCHA is solved, the server generates a random identifier, stores it in the cache for 15 minutes, and sends it to the browser in a cookie. The form is only displayed, and the account is only created, with a valid token; the token is consumed when the account is created. A solved CAPTCHA thus allows you to create an account, and typing the address [/inscription] directly will not work.

  • Lines 57–61: The cookie has the path [/inscription]; the browser sends it only to addresses that begin with this path. It is encrypted by [Laravel], like all cookies in the application except for two (see [bootstrap/app.php]): without the application’s key, no one can create a valid cookie or even read the identifier;
  • lines 64–67: To delete a cookie, you must specify the same name and the same path: to the browser, two cookies with the same name but different paths are considered two separate cookies.

docs.title: 11.12.7. Middleware: app/Http/Middleware
docs.text:
Three middleware components, located in the [app/Http/Middleware] folder, as is customary.

<?php
// app/Http/Middleware/FixerLangue.php: the request language (see example 22):
// the language of the [rdvmedecins_langue] cookie; if it is a supported language, French; otherwise, another language.
//
// A middleware GLOBAL (see bootstrap/app.php): it runs for TOUTES the
// requests, even those that do not result in a route (405 page...). It passes
// therefore passes through the EncryptCookies middleware of the [web] group, which decrypts the cookies:
// which is why the language cookie is excluded from encryption.

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\App;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class FixerLangue
{
     // the cookie that stores the selected language (see LangueController)
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_langue';

     // the supported languages (lang/fr.json, lang/en.json); the default is French
     // (config/app.php, locale key)
    public const LANGUES = ['fr', 'en'];

    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        $langue = $request->cookie(self::COOKIE);
        if (in_array($langue, self::LANGUES, true)) {
            App::setLocale($langue);
        }
        return $next($request);
    }
}

The request language (example 22): the language specified in the cookie, if it is a supported language; otherwise, the default language in the configuration (French). The languages and the cookie name are constants, for the same reason as the token cookie name. This middleware is global (see [bootstrap/app.php]).

<?php
// app/Http/Middleware/ExigerRoles.php: the user’s role must be one of
// those listed by the route; otherwise, a 403 response (an error page, see
// bootstrap/app.php). A middleware at PARAMÈTRES: in routes/web.php,
//    ->middleware('role:ADMIN,DOCTOR')
// calls handle($request, $next, 'ADMIN', 'DOCTOR') ; ...$roles receives them all.
//
// The authentication middleware (see bootstrap/app.php) is executed:
// The user is therefore known.

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use App\Web\Outils;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class ExigerRoles
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next, string ...$roles): Response
    {
        if (! in_array(Outils::utilisateur()->role->value, $roles, true)) {
            abort(403);
        }
        return $next($request);
    }
}

A middleware with parameters. In [routes/web.php], [->middleware('role:ADMIN,DOCTOR')] refers to the alias middleware [role] (see [bootstrap/app.php]), with two parameters: [Laravel] calls [handle($request, $next, 'ADMIN', 'DOCTOR')]. The variadic parameter [string ...$roles] receives all remaining parameters in an array (line 20). One role is missing from the list: 403 response ([abort(403)], Example 24). This is equivalent to the [can:admin] middleware from Example 26, without defining [Gate]: the application has only role rules. This middleware is always placed on routes protected by [Authenticate], which executes before it: [Authenticate] is part of the [web] group, whose middleware runs before that of the route. The user is therefore known.

<?php
// app/Http/Middleware/VerifierPasseInscription.php: GET and POST /registration
// require a valid token (see app/Auth/PasseInscription.php); otherwise,
// returns to the authentication page with a message. Entering URL directly
// /registration does not allow you to bypass the CAPTCHA.

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use App\Auth\PasseInscription;
use App\Web\Flash;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class VerifierPasseInscription
{
    public function __construct(private PasseInscription $passes)
    {
    }

    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        if (! $this->passes->estValide($request->cookie(PasseInscription::COOKIE))) {
            Flash::erreur('ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
            return redirect()->route('login');
        }
        return $next($request);
    }
}

No valid token: redirect to the login page with a message. The middleware receives the token service from its constructor: [Laravel] creates the middleware using the container, which provides them with their dependencies, just as it does for the controllers.

docs.title: 11.12.8. app/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php: the PUBLIQUES routes for the connection:
//    GE T         / redirects to the role's home page (or to /login)
//    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
//    POST /logi  n checks attempt limit, CAPTCHA, username/password
//    POST /logou t logs out
//
// Protection against bots, in this order:
//    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
//       -> immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
//    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Denied (counted as a failed attempt);
//    3. Only then is the password verified.
// The password for an attempt rejected in steps 1 or 2 is not verified:
// Therefore, a bot cannot learn anything by persisting.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Auth\AuthService;
use App\Auth\CaptchaService;
use App\Auth\LimiteurTentatives;
use App\Models\Role;
use App\Web\Message;
use Illuminate\Http\RedirectResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\View\View;

class AuthController
{
    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth,
        private CaptchaService $captchas,
        private LimiteurTentatives $limiteur,
    ) {
    }

     // The home page for each role, immediately after logging in
    public static function pageAccueil(Role $role): string
    {
        return $role === Role::USER ? route('espace') : route('agenda');
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /
     // The route is public: the user, if there is one, is known (Auth::user()),
     // but nothing is required.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function accueil(): RedirectResponse
    {
        $utilisateur = Auth::user();
        return redirect($utilisateur ? self::pageAccueil($utilisateur->role) : route('login'));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the login field
     // (used immediately after creating an account; see InscriptionController)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function formulaire(Request $request): View|RedirectResponse
    {
         // Already logged in (token still valid): goes directly to the home page
        if ($utilisateur = Auth::user()) {
            return redirect(self::pageAccueil($utilisateur->role));
        }
        return $this->page(Str::limit((string) $request->query('login', ''), 30, ''), null);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /login
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function connexion(Request $request): View|RedirectResponse
    {
        $login = (string) $request->input('login', '');
        $password = (string) $request->input('password', '');
        $ip = (string) $request->ip();

         // 1. Too many recent failed attempts?
        $minutes = $this->limiteur->minutesBlocageLogin($ip, $login);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]));
        }

         // 2. The CAPTCHA
        if (! $this->captchas->verifier($request->input('captchaId'), $request->input('captcha'))) {
            $this->limiteur->echecLogin($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA'));
        }

         // 3. The password
        $user = $login !== '' && $password !== '' ? $this->auth->valider($login, $password) : null;
        if ($user === null) {
            $this->limiteur->echecLogin($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('LOGIN.ERROR'));
        }

        $this->limiteur->reussiteLogin($ip, $login);
        return redirect(self::pageAccueil($user->role))->withCookie($this->auth->cookieJeton($user));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /logout: Clear the token cookie, then go to the login page.
     // POST only: a simple link (GET), placed on another site, cannot
     // log the user out without their knowledge.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function deconnexion(): RedirectResponse
    {
        return redirect()->route('login')->withCookie(AuthService::cookieEffacement());
    }

     // the form, always with a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used only once
     // time); the entered username is displayed again, but never the password
    private function page(string $login, ?Message $erreur): View
    {
        return view('login', ['titrePage' => 'LOGIN.TITLE', 'erreur' => $erreur, 'login' => $login,
            'captcha' => $this->captchas->generer()]);
    }
}

The connection controller, which is based on Example 27.

  • Lines 41–44: the home page for each role: “My Space” for a patient, the calendar for others. [route('espace')] generates the URL for the route named [espace] (Example 04);
  • lines 51–55: The address [/] redirects to the role’s home page or to the login page. The route is public: [Auth::user()] returns the user, if there is one, without requiring any input;
  • lines 61–68: A user who is already logged in goes directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] of URL pre-fills the field (after an account is created); [Str::limit] truncates it to 30 characters without adding anything (the third parameter, [''], replaces the usual ellipsis);
  • Lines 73–100: the login process, in the order shown in Example 27: potential blocking, the CAPTCHA, the password. A password is never verified for an attempt rejected by the limiter or the CAPTCHA: a bot learns nothing by persisting. In case of failure, the page is rendered directly (no redirection): the re-displayed form always has a new CAPTCHA and the entered login. The error is an object [Message] (see below), a key and its parameters, displayed at the bottom of the page. If successful, the login counter is reset to zero, and the browser is redirected to the role’s home page, with the token cookie ([withCookie]);
  • lines 107–110: Logout deletes the token cookie (example 25).

The login page receives the variable [titrePage], the translation key for the page title: all actions pass it to their view for the template (see below).

docs.title: 11.13. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: The [app/Web] folder contains the elements shared by the controllers.

docs.title: 11.13.1. app/Web/ApplicationModel.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Web/ApplicationModel.php: the cache/facade of the business layer (the equivalent
// to the [ApplicationModel] class in other versions of the application): the
// the lists of doctors and clients are retrieved from the database once, then served from
// the cache.
//
// Why use Laravel’s CACHE, and not simply a property of this object? Because
// an application PHP does not keep anything in memory from one request to the next: this
// object is a singleton (see AppServiceProvider), but a singleton only exists for the
// duration of a single UNE request. The cache, on the other hand, is shared by all requests (see
// examples 20 and 23).
//
// These lists can CHANGER (the ADMIN adds, modifies, or deletes doctors and
// clients): each write operation therefore goes through this facade, which OUBLIE the list
// immediately afterward; the next query that needs it reads it from the database. This is
// the whole point of an entry point UNIQUE to the business layer: the rule
// "write => cache update" is only written here.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;
use App\Metier\Metier;
use App\Metier\MetierService;
use App\Models\Client;
use App\Models\Creneau;
use App\Models\Medecin;
use App\Models\Rv;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;

// same contract as the business layer
class ApplicationModel implements Metier
{
    private const MEDECINS = 'rdvmedecins.medecins';

    private const CLIENTS = 'rdvmedecins.clients';

    public function __construct(private MetierService $metier)
    {
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

     // rememberForever: the value from the cache if it exists; otherwise, the function is
     // called, and its result stored in the cache (with no time limit) before
     // it is rendered
    public function getAllMedecins(): Collection
    {
        return Cache::rememberForever(self::MEDECINS, fn () => $this->metier->getAllMedecins());
    }

    public function getAllClients(): Collection
    {
        return Cache::rememberForever(self::CLIENTS, fn () => $this->metier->getAllClients());
    }

     // the doctor whose user account is [$idUser]—used to preselect,
     // for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar. firstWhere: the first element
     // in the collection whose property [user] is equal to $idUser
    public function getMedecinByUserId(int $idUser): ?Medecin
    {
        return $this->getAllMedecins()->firstWhere('user', $idUser);
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): Collection
    {
        return $this->metier->getAllCreneaux($idMedecin);
    }

    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): Collection
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client
    {
        return $this->metier->getClientById($id);
    }

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin
    {
        return $this->metier->getMedecinById($id);
    }

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvById($id);
    }

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau
    {
        return $this->metier->getCreneauById($id);
    }

    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, CarbonImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour
    {
        return $this->metier->getAgendaMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

     // no cache here: the most recent data is what counts (a patient who
     // has just modified or deleted their account)
    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client
    {
        return $this->metier->getClientByUserId($idUser);
    }

    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): Collection
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvAVenirClient($idClient);
    }

    public function ajouterRv(CarbonImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv
    {
        return $this->metier->ajouterRv($jour, $creneau, $client);
    }

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerRv($rv);
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ entries => cache ignored

    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return tap($this->metier->ajouterMedecin($donnees), fn () => Cache::forget(self::MEDECINS));
    }

    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return tap($this->metier->modifierMedecin($id, $donnees), fn () => Cache::forget(self::MEDECINS));
    }

    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerMedecin($id);
        Cache::forget(self::MEDECINS);
    }

    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return tap($this->metier->ajouterClient($donnees), fn () => Cache::forget(self::CLIENTS));
    }

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return tap($this->metier->modifierClient($id, $donnees), fn () => Cache::forget(self::CLIENTS));
    }

    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerClient($id);
        Cache::forget(self::CLIENTS);
    }
}

All versions of the application have a class named [ApplicationModel]: a single entry point from the web layer to the business layer, which keeps the lists of doctors and clients in memory. These lists are accessed by almost all pages (the drop-down list of doctors in the calendar, the list of patients in the booking window, and the administration pages) and rarely change.

What changes in [PHP] is the meaning of “in memory.” An application such as [Java], [C#], or [Python] remains in memory between requests; the [Flask] version stored these lists in the properties of a single object created at startup. An application [PHP] is recreated with each request (Example 01): the object [ApplicationModel] is indeed a singleton, but it exists only for the duration of a single request. The lists are therefore stored in the cache of [Laravel] (example 20), which is shared by all requests.

  • Lines 51–54: [Cache::rememberForever(clé, fonction)] returns the value stored under this key; if it does not exist, it calls the function (which reads the list from the database), stores its result in the cache indefinitely, and returns it. The first query that needs the list reads it from the database; subsequent queries find it in the cache. The cache stores the collection of objects [Eloquent] in a serialized form (Example 20) and reconstructs it upon reading, along with the loaded relationships (each person’s account);
  • lines 64–67: the doctor associated with an account, retrieved from the cache list: [firstWhere('user', $idUser)] returns the first element of the collection whose property [user] is equal to [$idUser];
  • lines 71–123: The other methods of the [Metier] contract simply delegate to the business layer. An account’s client ([getClientByUserId]) is always retrieved from the database, not from the cache: the most recent data is what matters (a patient who has just modified or deleted their account);
  • Lines 130–133 and following: the updates. Each write operation for a doctor or client clears the relevant list ([Cache::forget]): the next query that needs it will read it from the database again. [tap(valeur, fonction)] calls the function, then returns the value: in this case, the newly created doctor, after clearing the cache. This is the whole point of a single entry point: the rule “a write operation updates the cache” is defined only here. An application that writes to the database via a different path (another program, another version of the application using the same database) would leave the cache out of date: [php artisan cache:clear] would clear it.

docs.title: 11.13.2. app/Web/Message.php and Flash.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Web/Message.php: a message to translate: its key and its parameters.
// The views display it as {{ __($message->key, $message->parameters) }}.

namespace App\Web;

readonly class Message
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $cle,
        public array $parametres = [],
    ) {
    }
}

A message to be translated: a key and its parameters. Errors in the business layer ([MetierException]) and those in the controllers become [Message], which the views translate into the page’s language.

<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Web/Flash.php: “flash” messages: a message to be displayed UNE times on the
// SUIVANTE page (see Example 20). This is the natural complement to the
// "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all forms in the application: a
// successful POST does not generate a page; it redirects (302) to a GET page; the
// message, however, must survive the redirect.
//
// Laravel stores them in the SESSION, here in a CHIFFRÉ cookie (driver [cookie],
// see .env): the server does not retain anything between requests.
//
// A message does not contain text, but rather a translation CLÉ and its parameters:
// it is translated at the time of display, into the page’s language (see
// resources/views/fragments). Two lists: successes (displayed at the top of the
// page) and errors (displayed at the bottom).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

class Flash
{
    public static function succes(string $cle, array $parametres = []): void
    {
        self::ajouter('flash_succes', $cle, $parametres);
    }

    public static function erreur(string $cle, array $parametres = []): void
    {
        self::ajouter('flash_erreurs', $cle, $parametres);
    }

     // session()->flash(key, value): a value that is readable during the request
     // SUIVANTE only; it is populated if the current request has already set it
    private static function ajouter(string $liste, string $cle, array $parametres): void
    {
        $messages = session($liste, []);
        $messages[] = new Message($cle, $parametres);
        session()->flash($liste, $messages);
    }
}

Flash messages (example 20): a message stored in the session by an action, displayed by the next page, then discarded. This complements the Post/Redirect/Get pattern, which all forms in the application follow. Two lists, stored in the session under the keys [flash_succes] and [flash_erreurs]: success messages are displayed at the top of the page, and error messages at the bottom.

  • Lines 34–39: An action can store multiple messages: we append to the list already stored by the current request ([session($liste, [])] reads it, with an empty list by default), then store it again. [session()->flash(clé, valeur)] stores a value that will only persist until the end of the next request (example 20).

[Message] objects are stored as-is in the session: [Laravel] serializes the session data (Example 20) and reconstructs it during the next request. With the [cookie] driver (file [.env]), they are transmitted in an encrypted cookie.

docs.title: 11.13.3. app/Web/Outils.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Web/Outils.php: small utility functions for the web layer:
//    - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", days "Wednesday, September 23, 2026";
//    - input: reading a positive integer or a date sent by the browser;
//    - user: the logged-in user and their patient (Client entity).
// STATIQUES methods: these are called without creating an object (Tools::iso($jour)).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Auth\SessionInvalide;
use App\Auth\UtilisateurConnecte;
use App\Models\Client;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\App;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;

class Outils
{
     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

     // the date, if [$texte] is a valid date in the yyyy-mm-dd format; null otherwise.
     // createFromFormat accepts "2026-02-30" (which becomes March 2): we verify
     // so that the reconstructed date is written exactly as the received text
    public static function dateValide(?string $texte): ?CarbonImmutable
    {
        if ($texte === null || ! preg_match('/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/', $texte)) {
            return null;
        }
         // "!Y-m-d": the exclamation point sets the time to midnight
        $date = CarbonImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', $texte);
        return $date !== null && $date->format('Y-m-d') === $texte ? $date : null;
    }

    public static function iso(CarbonImmutable $jour): string
    {
        return $jour->format('Y-m-d');
    }

     // "Wednesday, September 23, 2026" / "mercredi 23 septembre 2026," depending on the language
     // of the query. isoFormat: dddd is the day of the week spelled out in full, D is the
     // day, MMMM the month spelled out, YYYY the year (see example 16)
    public static function formaterJour(CarbonImmutable $jour): string
    {
        return $jour->locale(App::getLocale())->isoFormat('dddd D MMMM YYYY');
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- input

     // "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", null -> null
    public static function entierPositif(mixed $valeur): ?int
    {
        if (! is_string($valeur) || ! preg_match('/^\d{1,9}$/', $valeur)) {
            return null;
        }
        $n = (int) $valeur;
        return $n > 0 ? $n : null;
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- user

     // the logged-in user. Protected actions are called only if it exists;
     // As a precaution, its absence is treated as an expired session
    public static function utilisateur(): UtilisateurConnecte
    {
        return Auth::user() ?? throw new SessionInvalide();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // The patient (Client entity) corresponding to the logged-in user.
    //
     // The token JWT contains only the ID of COMPTE (users.id). For a role USER,
     // the corresponding client is identified using the clients.user column.
    //
     // If there is no match, it means the account has been deleted since the login
     // even though its token is still valid: it is treated as an expired session
     // expired session (see SessionInvalide).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static function patientConnecte(ApplicationModel $application): Client
    {
        return $application->getClientByUserId(self::utilisateur()->userId)
            ?? throw new SessionInvalide();
    }
}

Some utility functions, in the form of static methods.

  • Lines 26–34: the date of a parameter [aaaa-mm-jj] or [null]. Two checks: the format (a regular expression), then the existence of the date. [createFromFormat] is lenient: February 30 becomes March 2. We therefore re-read the resulting date and verify that it is written exactly as the received text. The [!] in the format sets the time to midnight (without it, the time would be the current time);
  • Lines 44–47: “Saturday, September 26, 2026” or “Saturday 26 September 2026,” depending on the language of the query. [isoFormat] (example 16) uses the format codes from the [JavaScript] [Moment.js] library: [dddd], the day of the week spelled out; [D], the day; [MMMM], the month spelled out; [YYYY], the year. [locale(...)] returns a copy of the date set for a specific language;
  • lines 52–59: a query parameter is a string, or [null], or even an array ([?idMedecin[]=1], example 10). Only digits are accepted (up to nine: no overflow), and the number must be strictly positive. [mixed]: any type;
  • lines 65–68: the logged-in user. [Auth::user()] returns [null] for an anonymous visitor; protected actions are only called for an authenticated user, but the absence of a user is still handled as an expired session;
  • lines 80–84: the patient ([Client]) of the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID; the client is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, the account has been deleted since the user logged in: [SessionInvalide].

docs.title: 11.14. The dictionaries
docs.text:
The interface texts are the same as those in other versions of the application, which stored them in nested JSON files:

{
  "LOGIN": {
    "TITLE": "Connexion",
    ...
  }
}

The [Flask] version “flattened” them at startup: [LOGIN.TITLE] referred to the text in [Connexion]. [Laravel] reads flat JSON dictionaries (example 22), where the key is the text to be translated or an identifier: We have flattened the dictionaries once and for all, and replaced the [{nom}] parameters from other versions with the notation used in [Laravel] and [:nom]:

{
    "APP.TITLE": "RdvMedecins",
    "APP.LOGOUT": "Se déconnecter",
    ...
    "MEDECINS.ADDED": "Le médecin :nom a été ajouté (login : :login).",
    ...
}

The files [lang/fr.json] and [lang/en.json] each contain 153 texts; they are not reproduced here. A key is represented by [__('APP.LOGOUT')], and a parameterized text by [__('MEDECINS.ADDED', ['nom' => ..., 'login' => ...])]. [Laravel] first searches for the complete key in the language’s dictionary, JSON; if it does not find it, it searches for it in the [PHP] files in the [lang/fr] folder (example 09); if that fails, it displays the key itself, which immediately signals an omission. A text entry has been added: [ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED], the message on page 419, which is not present in the other versions.

docs.title: 11.15. Forms
docs.text: "Person" forms are validated by form requests ([FormRequest], example 19): classes that describe the validation rules for a request. Let’s review the principle: an action that receives a [FormRequest] as a parameter is called only if the input is valid; otherwise, [Laravel] redirects the browser back to the form page, along with error messages ([$errors] in the view) and the input to be redisplayed ([old('champ')]), excluding passwords.

docs.title: 11.15.1. app/Http/Requests/ChampsPersonneRequest.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// app/Http/Requests/ChampsPersonneRequest.php: the form fields
// "person" and their validation rules (see Example 19). Three forms
// share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//    ChampsPersonneReques         t title, first name, last name
//     ├─ PersonneReque           st + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
//                                    │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
//     ├─ InscriptionReque        st + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
//                                    │ (a patient creates an account)
//     └─ MonCompteReque          st + username, optional new password,
//                                     password ACTUEL required, version
//                                     (a patient modifies their account)
//
// A class ABSTRAITE: it is never used on its own; its child classes complete
// its rules (array_merge) and its messages.
//
// Reminders (Example 19): An action that receives a FormRequest as a parameter is
// called only if the input is valid; otherwise, Laravel redirects the browser to
// the form page (redirect), along with the error messages ($errors in the
// view) and the input to be redisplayed (old('field'))—JAMAIS passwords.
// The messages are the texts from the lang/*.json dictionaries: __('ERRORS...').
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;

abstract class ChampsPersonneRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

     // login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
    public const FORMAT_LOGIN = '/^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/';

     // Minimum password length for a patient: CHOISI
    public const MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6;

     // Before validation: a username is always in lowercase. Unnecessary spaces
     // have already been removed from all fields by the Laravel middleware
     // TrimStrings from Laravel—except for passwords (password,
     // password_confirmation, current_password), which may contain them; an
     // an empty field has become null (ConvertEmptyStringsToNull middleware)
    protected function prepareForValidation(): void
    {
        if (is_string($this->input('login'))) {
            $this->merge(['login' => Str::lower($this->input('login'))]);
        }
    }

     // rule: validation of a field stops at the first rule that is not met—
     // Only one message per field. Maximum lengths = those of the columns SQL
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'titre' => ['bail', 'required', Rule::in(self::TITRES)],
            'prenom' => ['bail', 'required', 'string', 'max:20'],
            'nom' => ['bail', 'required', 'string', 'max:20'],
        ];
    }

     // champ.règle -> message
    public function messages(): array
    {
        return [
            'titre' => __('ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE'),
            'prenom.required' => __('ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED'),
            'prenom' => __('ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
            'nom.required' => __('ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED'),
            'nom' => __('ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
            'login.required' => __('ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED'),
            'login' => __('ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN'),
            'password.required' => __('ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED'),
            'password.min' => __('ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT', ['min' => self::MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN]),
            'password' => __('ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG'),
            'password_confirmation.required' => __('ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED'),
            'password_confirmation' => __('ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER'),
            'current_password' => __('ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED'),
            'version' => __('ERRORS.INVALID_FORM'),
        ];
    }

     // the version (optimistic lock), if the form has one
    public function version(): ?int
    {
        return $this->filled('version') ? (int) $this->input('version') : null;
    }
}

Three forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name): the administrator form (for a doctor or a client), the client account creation form, and “Manage My Account.” Their common parent class is abstract; each of its child classes extends its rules.

  • lines 34–40: the input rules, in the form of constants, which are also read by the views (the list of titles);
  • Lines 47–52: [prepareForValidation] is called before validation: the input can be transformed there. A login is always in lowercase: [merge] replaces the field value in the query. The other validations are already performed by two global middleware components of [Laravel] (see the chapter on the lifecycle): [TrimStrings] removes leading and trailing spaces from all values, except those in fields [password], [password_confirmation], and [current_password] (spaces may be part of a password); [ConvertEmptyStringsToNull] replaces an empty string with [null]. This is why the password fields in the application have these names, which correspond to the usage of [Laravel];
  • Lines 56–63: the rules for the three fields. [bail] stops validating a field as soon as the first rule is violated: only one message per field. [Rule::in(...)]: the value must be one of those in the list. [max:20]: 20 characters maximum; the column length is defined by SQL;
  • lines 66–84: error messages, taken from the dictionaries. The key ['prenom.required'] refers to the message for rule [required] in field [prenom]; the key ['prenom'] alone refers to the message for all other rules in this field. The message for a rule is first looked up under the key [champ.règle], then under the key [règle] (the message for this rule for all fields), and then under the key [champ]. The child rules (login, passwords) have their messages here: an unused message does not cause any issues. The method [messages] is called during validation, in the language of the request;
  • lines 87–90: the version (the hidden field for the optimistic lock), as an integer, or [null] if the field is empty or absent. [filled]: the field is present and not empty.

docs.title: 11.15.2. app/Http/Requests/PersonneRequest.php, InscriptionRequest.php, MonCompteRequest.php
docs.text:
<?php
// app/Http/Requests/PersonneRequest.php: a doctor’s or client’s form
// (ADMIN): FACULTATIFS login and password (see app/Metier/DonneesPersonne.php).

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;

class PersonneRequest extends ChampsPersonneRequest
{
     // nullable: an empty (null) field is accepted, without checking the other rules
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return array_merge(parent::rules(), [
            'login' => ['bail', 'nullable', 'string', 'regex:'.self::FORMAT_LOGIN],
             // Maximum 72 characters: if longer, bcrypt ignores the rest
            'password' => ['bail', 'nullable', 'string', 'max:72'],
             // hidden field in the update form (optimistic lock)
            'version' => ['nullable', 'integer'],
        ]);
    }

     // Validated input -> data expected by the business layer
    public function donnees(): DonneesPersonne
    {
        return new DonneesPersonne($this->input('titre'), $this->input('nom'), $this->input('prenom'),
            $this->input('login'), $this->input('password'), $this->version());
    }
}

The administrator form. [array_merge] adds three rules to those of the parent class: the username and password are optional ([nullable]: the value [null] is accepted, and the other rules are then not checked); [regex:...] validates the format of the username; [max:72] limits the length of a password: [bcrypt] considers only the first 72 bytes (example 25). The [donnees] method (lines 24–28) converts the validated input into [DonneesPersonne] for the business layer: the business layer does not recognize HTTP requests.

<?php
// app/Http/Requests/InscriptionRequest.php: "Create a customer account": username, password
// password and confirmation OBLIGATOIRES.

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;

class InscriptionRequest extends ChampsPersonneRequest
{
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return array_merge(parent::rules(), [
            'login' => ['bail', 'required', 'string', 'regex:'.self::FORMAT_LOGIN],
            'password' => ['bail', 'required', 'string', 'min:'.self::MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, 'max:72'],
             // same:password: The confirmation must match the password
            'password_confirmation' => ['bail', 'required', 'same:password'],
        ]);
    }

    public function donnees(): DonneesPersonne
    {
        return new DonneesPersonne($this->input('titre'), $this->input('nom'), $this->input('prenom'),
            $this->input('login'), $this->input('password'));
    }
}

Creating a customer account: login and password are required, and the password must be confirmed. The rule [same:password] requires that the field [password_confirmation] have the same value as the field [password]; its message (“The confirmation does not match the password. ”) appears below the confirmation field. [Laravel] also has a rule, [confirmed], which checks the same thing but based on the [password] field; its message would appear below the password field.

<?php
// app/Http/Requests/MonCompteRequest.php: "Manage My Account" (a patient): username
// required, new password optional, password ACTUEL required.

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;

class MonCompteRequest extends ChampsPersonneRequest
{
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return array_merge(parent::rules(), [
            'login' => ['bail', 'required', 'string', 'regex:'.self::FORMAT_LOGIN],
             // optional: blank = password unchanged
            'password' => ['bail', 'nullable', 'string', 'min:'.self::MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, 'max:72'],
            'password_confirmation' => ['same:password'],
             // the password ACTUEL, required for any account changes
            'current_password' => ['required'],
            'version' => ['nullable', 'integer'],
        ]);
    }

    public function donnees(): DonneesPersonne
    {
        return new DonneesPersonne($this->input('titre'), $this->input('nom'), $this->input('prenom'),
            $this->input('login'), $this->input('password'), $this->version());
    }
}

“Manage My Account”: The new password is optional (leave blank to keep the current password), and the current password is required. The rule [same:password] applies even to an empty confirmation field: if a new password is entered, the confirmation must also be entered. The current password is not verified here, but by the action: an incorrect password must be counted by the attempt limiter as a failed login. [Laravel] has a rule, [current_password], which compares the entered password to the logged-in user’s password; this rule is not suitable here: our logged-in user ([UtilisateurConnecte]) does not contain the hash of their password.

docs.title: 11.16. View Templates
docs.text:
The [app/Vues] folder contains the view templates: objects created by an action, which the view simply reads. The rule followed by all pages is: no logic in the views. The actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views place them in the HTML. All these classes are [readonly] and have only properties, which are promoted by their constructor.

<?php
// app/Vues/OptionVue.php: an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient).
//
// The app/Views folder contains the "view models": objects
// constructed once by an action, which the view simply reads. Rule
// followed by all pages: no logic in the views. The actions
// prepare formatted data DÉJÀ (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,”
// "8:00 - 8:20", selection = true...) and already filtered according to the user’s
// the user; the views simply place them in the HTML.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class OptionVue
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $id,
        public string $libelle,
        public bool $selectionne,
    ) {
    }
}

An option in a drop-down list: the ID, the label, and whether the option is selected?

<?php
// app/Views/LigneAgenda.php: a row in the displayed calendar (a time slot).

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class LigneAgenda
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $idCreneau,
        public string $horaire,      // "8:00 - 8:20"
        public bool $libre,
         // displayed name for a booked time slot; null = “Reserved”
        public ?string $patient,
        public bool $moi,            // the appointment for the logged-in patient
        public bool $reservable,     // Display the "Book" button?
        public string $urlReserver,
         // filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
        public ?int $idRv,
    ) {
    }
}

An entry in the calendar: a time slot, and what the logged-in user is authorized to view and do with it. [patient] is populated only if the user has permission to view the patient’s name; [reservable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [idRv] indicates whether to display the “Cancel” button.

<?php
// app/Views/AgendaVue.php: the displayed calendar: doctor, day, rows.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class AgendaVue
{
     /** @param list<LigneAgenda> $lignes */
    public function __construct(
        public string $medecin,      // "Ms. Marie PELISSIER"
        public string $jour,         // "Wednesday, September 23, 2026"
        public array $lignes,
    ) {
    }
}

<?php
// app/Views/ReservationVue.php: the slot reservation window.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class ReservationVue
{
     /** @param list<OptionVue> $clients */
    public function __construct(
        public int $idCreneau,
        public string $horaire,
         // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the patients to choose from
        public array $clients,
         // USER: the patient is the patient himself
        public ?string $patient,
    ) {
    }
}

The displayed calendar and the booking window: for the administrator and doctors, the list of patients to choose from; for a patient, their own name.

<?php
// app/Views/ClesPersonnes.php: translation keys specific to each type of
// person (doctors or clients), for the common people/list views and
// "People/Form" views.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class ClesPersonnes
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $titre,                 // "Doctors"
        public string $ajouter,               // "Add a doctor"
        public string $modifier,              // "Edit a doctor"
        public string $vide,                  // "No doctors."
        public string $confirmerSuppression,  // "Delete this doctor...?"
        public string $ajoute,                // "The doctor:name has been added (login: :login)."
        public string $modifie,
        public string $supprime,
    ) {
    }

     // the eight keys of a dictionary section ("MEDECINS", "CLIENTS")
    public static function de(string $section): self
    {
        return new self("$section.TITLE", "$section.ADD", "$section.EDIT", "$section.EMPTY",
            "$section.DELETE_CONFIRM", "$section.ADDED", "$section.UPDATED", "$section.DELETED");
    }
}

The translation keys specific to doctors or clients, for the two views they have in common. The static method [de] (lines 23–27) generates the eight keys for a section of the dictionaries: [ClesPersonnes::de('MEDECINS')] yields [MEDECINS.TITLE], [MEDECINS.ADD]... [new self(...)] creates an object of the class itself.

<?php
// app/Views/RendezVousVue.php: an upcoming appointment in the patient’s dashboard.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class RendezVousVue
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $id,
        public string $jour,         // "Wednesday, September 23, 2026"
        public string $horaire,      // "8:00 - 8:20"
        public string $medecin,      // "Ms. Marie PELISSIER"

An upcoming appointment in the patient area.

docs.title: 11.17. The web layer: routes and controllers
11.17.1. routes/web.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// routes/web.php: all URL entries in the application.
//
// Reminder (see bootstrap/app.php): all these routes require a user
// authenticated user; SAUF those in the first group, which remove the middleware
// authentication middleware (withoutMiddleware). The middleware [role:...] also requires
// one of the listed roles; it applies to a route, or to all routes in a
// group.
//
// ->name(...): the NOM of the route, which the code uses to generate its URL
// (route('agenda', [...]), redirect()->route('login')...) : changing a URL does not
// requires modifying only this file.
// =========================================================================

use App\Http\Controllers\AgendaController;
use App\Http\Controllers\AuthController;
use App\Http\Controllers\ClientsController;
use App\Http\Controllers\EspaceController;
use App\Http\Controllers\InscriptionController;
use App\Http\Controllers\LangueController;
use App\Http\Controllers\MedecinsController;
use App\Http\Middleware\FixerLangue;
use Illuminate\Auth\Middleware\Authenticate;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the routes PUBLIQUES
Route::withoutMiddleware(Authenticate::class)->group(function () {
     // Login (see AuthController)
    Route::controller(AuthController::class)->group(function () {
        Route::get('/', 'accueil')->name('accueil');
        Route::get('login', 'formulaire')->name('login');
        Route::post('login', 'connexion');
        Route::post('logout', 'deconnexion')->name('logout');
    });

     // language selection: /language/fr, /language/en; any other value: 404
    Route::get('langue/{code}', [LangueController::class, 'changer'])
        ->whereIn('code', FixerLangue::LANGUES)->name('langue');

     // creating a customer account (see InscriptionController); the form
     // requires a token (middleware passe.inscription)
    Route::controller(InscriptionController::class)->prefix('inscription')->group(function () {
        Route::post('acces', 'acces')->name('inscription.acces');
        Route::middleware('passe.inscription')->group(function () {
            Route::get('', 'formulaire')->name('inscription');
            Route::post('', 'creer');
        });
    });

     // no other route matches the requested URL: 404 page. A
     // "fallback" rather than Laravel’s automatic 404: the request is thus passed
     // through the middleware in the [web] group (session, user...), and the
     // error page has its full navigation bar
    Route::fallback(fn () => abort(404));
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the calendar (all roles)
Route::controller(AgendaController::class)->prefix('agenda')->group(function () {
    Route::get('', 'afficher')->name('agenda');
    Route::post('reserver', 'reserver')->middleware('role:ADMIN,DOCTOR,USER')->name('agenda.reserver');
     // A patient cancels SON an appointment from “My Account,” not from here
    Route::post('annuler', 'annuler')->middleware('role:ADMIN,DOCTOR')->name('agenda.annuler');
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- doctors and clients (ADMIN)
// Both sections have the MÊMES routes (see PersonnesController): a loop declares them
// is declared for each one. The route names are prefixed with the section:
// medecins.liste, clients.liste...
foreach (['medecins' => MedecinsController::class, 'clients' => ClientsController::class] as $section => $controleur) {
    Route::controller($controleur)->prefix($section)->name("$section.")->middleware('role:ADMIN')
        ->group(function () {
            Route::get('', 'liste')->name('liste');
            Route::get('ajouter', 'formulaireAjout')->name('ajout');
            Route::post('ajouter', 'ajouter')->name('ajouter');
             // whereNumber: {id} must consist of digits
            Route::get('{id}/modifier', 'formulaireModification')->whereNumber('id')->name('modification');
            Route::post('{id}/modifier', 'modifier')->whereNumber('id')->name('modifier');
            Route::post('{id}/supprimer', 'supprimer')->whereNumber('id')->name('supprimer');
        });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the patient's space (USER)
Route::controller(EspaceController::class)->middleware('role:USER')->group(function () {
    Route::get('mon-espace', 'espace')->name('espace');
    Route::post('mon-espace/annuler', 'annulerRv')->name('espace.annuler');
    Route::get('mon-compte', 'formulaireCompte')->name('compte');
    Route::post('mon-compte', 'modifierCompte')->name('compte.modifier');
    Route::post('mon-compte/supprimer', 'supprimerCompte')->name('compte.supprimer');
});

All URL routes in the application. Note that all these routes require an authenticated user (the [Authenticate] middleware, added to the [web] group by [bootstrap/app.php]), except for those that remove this requirement.

  • Lines 28–56: the public routes. [withoutMiddleware] removes a middleware component from the routes in the group: in this case, authentication. These include login ([AuthController]), language selection, and customer account creation;
  • Lines 30–35: [Route::controller] (Example 02) specifies the controller for the group’s routes: each route now names only its method. [->name('login')] assigns a name to the route (Example 04): the code generates its URL files using this name ([route('login')], [redirect()->route('login')]), and changing a URL file requires modifying only that file. The name [login] also has significance for [Laravel]: it is the page to which the [Authenticate] middleware redirects an anonymous visitor if no other page is specified;
  • lines 38–39: [whereIn('code', [...])] accepts only the values in the list for the [{code}] parameter: [/langue/de] does not correspond to any route (404 page);
  • lines 43–49: account creation. [prefix('inscription')] adds [/inscription] before the URL entries in the group: [Route::get('', ...)] is the [/inscription] route itself. The form (GET and POST) also requires a pass: the alias middleware [passe.inscription];
  • line 55: the fallback route, selected when no other route matches a request for GET. Without it, [Laravel] itself generates a 404 error before the middleware in the [web] group is executed: no session, no decrypted cookies... The error page would have neither the user’s name in its navigation bar nor an anti-CSRF token for the logout button. With the fallback route, the request passes through the [web] group, and then the action raises a 404 error. The route is public: an unknown address returns a 404 page, even to an anonymous visitor. Side effect: a request from GET to URL, which exists only as POST ([/logout]) also returns a 404 page, not a 405;
  • lines 59–64: the calendar. Its page is accessible to all authenticated users; booking is available to the three roles (i.e., any authenticated user; the list of roles documents this rule); cancellation is available to the administrator and doctors: [->middleware('role:ADMIN,DOCTOR')];
  • lines 70–81: The routes for doctors and clients are the same: a loop declares them for each of the two sections. The routes file is a standard [PHP] file: you can write loops, conditions, and functions in it. For each section, there is a group: the controller, the URL prefix ([/medecins]), the name prefix ([->name("$section.")]: the route named [liste] is called [medecins.liste]), and the middleware [role:ADMIN], which protects all routes in the group—including those added later. [whereNumber('id')] accepts only numbers for the [{id}] parameter (e.g., 02);
  • lines 84–90: the patient area, reserved for the USER role.

The URL codes correspond to other versions of the application: modifying and deleting a physician are POST requests ([/medecins/{id}/modifier], [/medecins/{id}/supprimer]), not PUT and DELETE as in Example 28. The [php artisan route:list] command displays the list of routes, along with their names and actions.
